surfaced as a product feature in redwood console and via the redwood api as an opt - in routing and fidelity negotiation layer. key problem we solve : - customers must choose between maintaining strict latency slos or using higher - fidelity, higher - cost model variants. - manual variant selection and static capacity reservations lead to excess cost or sla violations during traffic spikes. - developers need a simple contract to express latency versus quality priorities per route. primary personas : - platform engineers at mid - market and enterprise customers who set per - route slas and want predictable latency for user - facing features. - product / ml engineers at startups who want low - latency defaults without deep runtime tuning. - redwood sales and solutions engineers who sell dedicated / private packages with sla add - ons.

# Platform & Console knowledge brief

Platform & Console owns inference gateway policy, tenant configuration, safe rollouts, telemetry workflows, and the operator-facing console. The team uses LiteLLM for gateway work and Langfuse for observability and console workflows, reconciling code changes with product, security, and operational requirements.

# committers this document lists the current committers of the vllm project and the core areas they maintain. committers have write access to the vllm repository and are responsible for reviewing and merging prs. you can also refer to the [ codeowners ] ( https : / / github. com / vllm - project / vllm / blob / main /. github / codeowners ) file for concrete file - level ownership and reviewers. both this documents and the codeowners file are living documents and they complement each other. # # active committers

document.title: Platform & Console knowledge brief
document.content:
# Platform & Console knowledge brief

Platform & Console owns inference gateway policy, tenant configuration, safe rollouts, telemetry workflows, and the operator-facing console. The team uses LiteLLM for gateway work and Langfuse for observability and console workflows, reconciling code changes with product, security, and operational requirements.

## High-value source areas

These are retrieval hints, not access-control filters.

- codebases/litellm
- codebases/langfuse
- github/rbac-policy-bundle
- linear/engineering
- linear/design
- confluence/eng-platform
- confluence/product-docs
- slack/eng-platform
- slack/product

Lead: Priya Natarajan

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_be4b992c9bd941c5942e600ef769f6e4",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/first-week-systems-and-badge-onboarding-playbook-2024.json",
    "title": "First Week Systems & Badge Onboarding Playbook",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"First Week Systems & Badge Onboarding Playbook\",\n  \"space\": \"company-handbook\",\n  \"author\": \"Marisol Chen\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"people-ops\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-10-20\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2025-06-18\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Jordan Lee\",\n    \"Priya Natarajan\",\n    \"Samir Gupta\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"onboarding\",\n    \"tools\",\n    \"access\",\n    \"badge\",\n    \"first-week\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/path-to-impact-new-hire-120-day-ops-and-benefit-orientation-2023\",\n    \"/confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/onboarding-toolchain-access-and-career-checkpoints-2025\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"content\": \"Overview\\n\\nThis playbook describes the recommended, low-friction process for new hires to obtain systems access, physical badge entry, and the core toolchain needed to be productive in their first week. It is intended for people-ops partners, hiring managers, IT/staff engineers, and hiring-team buddies who coordinate access. The emphasis is on automated flows, clear owners, and fallback runbooks for common failures.\\n\\nIntended outcomes (by the end of week 1)\\n- Employee has building badge and primary laptop configured.\\n- Access to core cloud projects, code repositories, and primary communication tools (Slack, email, calendar).\\n- Access requests are auditable and issued with minimum-privilege roles.\\n- New hire is able to run the local dev quickstart and join at least one team-sync.\\n\\nOwners & escalation\\n- Primary owner: people-ops (badge logistics, orientation scheduling)\\n- Systems owner: IT Ops / Staff Engineer on-call (laptop imaging, VPN/KMS)\\n- Access control and IAM: Security team (RBAC policy exceptions)\\n- Escalation path: People-ops -> IT Ops -> Security -> CTO on emergent risk items\\n\\nBefore day 0 (People-ops checklist)\\n1. Confirm start date and work location; schedule badge pickup (if office) and shipping of laptop (if remote).\\n2. Pre-provision SSO account and temporary Slack invite.\\n3. Generate onboarding access bundle: initial repo access list, cloud project names, and team-specific infra tickets.\\n4. Create calendar invites for orientation, manager 1:1, and buddy sessions.\\n\\nDay 0 / Pre-boarding automated tasks\\n- Trigger account creation job: run `onboard create-account --email <email> --team <team-slug> --start <YYYY-MM-DD>`\\n- Auto-approve baseline access role: `roles:employee-basic` (access to internal wiki, Slack, and email).\\n- Push laptop image to courier or on-site pick-up location.\\n\\nDay 1 checklist (manager + buddy)\\n1. Welcome meeting and orientation (walkthrough of this playbook)\\n2. Badge pickup / building entry verification (if on-site): bring government ID; sign H&S brief.\\n3. Verify SSO login and MFA enrollment. If failure, escalate to IT Ops (see troubleshooting).\\n4. Confirm Slack and email deliverability.\\n5. Validate access to source control and package manager: run the quick test in the `quickstarts/new-hire` repo.\\n6. Run a smoke test with the team\\u2019s canonical dev environment (local or cloud).\\n7. Confirm calendar and team workspace membership.\\n\\nCore systems access table (summary)\\n| System | Typical initial role | Owner | Time to grant (SLA) | Notes |\\n|--------|----------------------|-------|----------------------|-------|\\n| Single Sign-On (SSO) | employee-basic | people-ops | 0-4h | MFA mandatory; include recovery options |\\n| Slack | member | people-ops | 0-2h | Auto-joins primary team channel |\\n| Email & Calendar | standard mailbox | people-ops | 0-2h | Auto-forward rules for manager |\\n| Source control (git.redwood) | repo-read | hiring manager | <24h | Managers request additional repos via PR |\\n| Cloud project (dev) | viewer | infra team | <24h | Bump to editor via infra ticket |\\n| Internal VPN | vpn-user | IT Ops | 0-8h | Required for private regions; certificate-based |\\n| Badge / Physical access | building-level | Facilities/People-ops | 1-3 business days | Expedited pickup available with manager note |\\n\\nNotes about the table: the above is a human-readable summary. Individual repos, cloud projects, and sensitive services require explicit tickets or role approvals. Use least privilege by default.\\n\\nCommon first-week operations (how-to)\\n- Request additional repository access: open `Access Request` in the IT portal, fill repo name and justification, tag manager and security reviewer. Typical flow: manager approves -> auto-grant script runs -> audit log entry created.\\n- Request production access: production access requires a documented justification and a security review. Use template in the IT portal and attach the rollout plan.\\n\\nTroubleshooting checklist (frequent failures)\\n- SSO login fails: ensure new hire registered authenticator; run `auth-tool verify --user <email>` and check error codes. If `ERR_MFA_NOT_ENROLLED`, instruct to register via SSO URL; if `ERR_USER_NOT_FOUND` escalate to people-ops.\\n- Laptop imaging failed: escalate to IT Ops; temporary loaner policy applies (loaner devices available for <= 14 days).\\n- Badge not programmed: verify employee ID in facility system, then request reissue with Facilities ticket `FAC-ISSUE-BADGE` and tag People-ops.\\n\\nAutomations and CLI snippets\\n- Pre-provision role and repo access (people-ops):\\n  `onboard preprovision --email maria@example.com --teams infra,eng --repos team-repo,shared-lib`\\n- Manager grant pattern (for recurring contractors):\\n  `access-request create --user contractor@example.com --scopes \\\"repo:team-repo:write\\\" --expires 2025-04-30`\\n\\nSecurity & compliance guidance\\n- All initial accounts are created with time-limited default roles; any permanent elevation requires a documented business case.\\n- Audit logs for access grants are retained for 365 days.\\n- Physical badge provisioning must be linked to a signed offer and background check clearance for roles that require secure-zone access.\\n\\nFirst-week success signals (manager report)\\n- New hire completed quickstart and opened their first PR.\\n- New hire is in calendar and Slack, attended at least 3 team events.\\n- No unresolved access blockers older than 48 hours.\\n\\nAppendix A: Access request template (copy into IT portal)\\n- Requester: <manager-name>\\n- Employee: <employee-name>\\n- Start date: <YYYY-MM-DD>\\n- Systems required: <list>\\n- Justification: <short description>\\n- Expiration: <YYYY-MM-DD or none>\\n\\nAppendix B: Emergency escalation contacts\\n- People-ops pager: people-ops@redwood.example.com (watch: 9am-6pm PT)\\n- IT Ops on-call: it-oncall@redwood.example.com (24/7)\\n- Security incident inbox: sec-ops@redwood.example.com\\n\\nRelated documentation\\n- See: /confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/manager-first-90-and-career-mobility-playbook-2026 for manager-facing onboarding rhythms.\\n- See: /confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/onboarding-toolchain-access-and-career-checkpoints-2025 for toolchain-specific deep dives.\\n\\nRevision history\\n- 2024-10-20: First draft created by Marisol Chen.\\n- 2025-06-18: Revised to add CLI snippets and updated badge SLA (Marisol Chen).\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_be4b992c9bd941c5942e600ef769f6e4\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: First Week Systems & Badge Onboarding Playbook\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/first-week-systems-and-badge-onboarding-playbook-2024.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: company-handbook\n\nproduction access requires a documented justification and a security review. use template in the it portal and attach the rollout plan. troubleshooting checklist ( frequent failures ) - sso login fails : ensure new hire registered authenticator ; run ` auth - tool verify - - user < email > ` and check error codes. if ` err _ mfa _ not _ enrolled `, instruct to register via sso url ; if ` err _ user _ not _ found ` escalate to people - ops. - laptop imaging failed : escalate to it ops ; temporary loaner policy applies ( loaner devices available for < = 14 days ). - badge not programmed : verify employee id in facility system, then request reissue with facilities ticket ` fac - issue - badge ` and tag people - ops.",

{
  "title": "First Week Systems & Badge Onboarding Playbook",
  "space": "company-handbook",
  "author": "Marisol Chen",
  "owner_team": "people-ops",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2024-10-20",
  "last_updated": "2025-06-18",
  "reviewers": [
    "Jordan Lee",
    "Priya Natarajan",
    "Samir Gupta"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "onboarding",
    "tools",
    "access",
    "badge",
    "first-week"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/path-to-impact-new-hire-120-day-ops-and-benefit-orientation-2023",
    "/confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/onboarding-toolchain-access-and-career-checkpoints-2025"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "content": "Overview

This playbook describes the recommended, low-friction process for new hires to obtain systems access, physical badge entry, and the core toolchain needed to be productive in their first week. It is intended for people-ops partners, hiring managers, IT/staff engineers, and hiring-team buddies who coordinate access. The emphasis is on automated flows, clear owners, and fallback runbooks for common failures.

Intended outcomes (by the end of week 1)
- Employee has building badge and primary laptop configured.
- Access to core cloud projects, code repositories, and primary communication tools (Slack, email, calendar).
- Access requests are auditable and issued with minimum-privilege roles.
- New hire is able to run the local dev quickstart and join at least one team-sync.

Owners & escalation
- Primary owner: people-ops (badge logistics, orientation scheduling)
- Systems owner: IT Ops / Staff Engineer on-call (laptop imaging, VPN/KMS)
- Access control and IAM: Security team (RBAC policy exceptions)
- Escalation path: People-ops -> IT Ops -> Security -> CTO on emergent risk items

Before day 0 (People-ops checklist)
1. Confirm start date and work location; schedule badge pickup (if office) and shipping of laptop (if remote).
2. Pre-provision SSO account and temporary Slack invite.
3. Generate onboarding access bundle: initial repo access list, cloud project names, and team-specific infra tickets.
4. Create calendar invites for orientation, manager 1:1, and buddy sessions.

Day 0 / Pre-boarding automated tasks
- Trigger account creation job: run `onboard create-account --email <email> --team <team-slug> --start <YYYY-MM-DD>`
- Auto-approve baseline access role: `roles:employee-basic` (access to internal wiki, Slack, and email).
- Push laptop image to courier or on-site pick-up location.

Day 1 checklist (manager + buddy)
1. Welcome meeting and orientation (walkthrough of this playbook)
2. Badge pickup / building entry verification (if on-site): bring government ID; sign H&S brief.
3. Verify SSO login and MFA enrollment. If failure, escalate to IT Ops (see troubleshooting).
4. Confirm Slack and email deliverability.
5. Validate access to source control and package manager: run the quick test in the `quickstarts/new-hire` repo.
6. Run a smoke test with the team’s canonical dev environment (local or cloud).
7. Confirm calendar and team workspace membership.

Core systems access table (summary)
| System | Typical initial role | Owner | Time to grant (SLA) | Notes |
|--------|----------------------|-------|----------------------|-------|
| Single Sign-On (SSO) | employee-basic | people-ops | 0-4h | MFA mandatory; include recovery options |
| Slack | member | people-ops | 0-2h | Auto-joins primary team channel |
| Email & Calendar | standard mailbox | people-ops | 0-2h | Auto-forward rules for manager |
| Source control (git.redwood) | repo-read | hiring manager | <24h | Managers request additional repos via PR |
| Cloud project (dev) | viewer | infra team | <24h | Bump to editor via infra ticket |
| Internal VPN | vpn-user | IT Ops | 0-8h | Required for private regions; certificate-based |
| Badge / Physical access | building-level | Facilities/People-ops | 1-3 business days | Expedited pickup available with manager note |

Notes about the table: the above is a human-readable summary. Individual repos, cloud projects, and sensitive services require explicit tickets or role approvals. Use least privilege by default.

Common first-week operations (how-to)
- Request additional repository access: open `Access Request` in the IT portal, fill repo name and justification, tag manager and security reviewer. Typical flow: manager approves -> auto-grant script runs -> audit log entry created.
- Request production access: production access requires a documented justification and a security review. Use template in the IT portal and attach the rollout plan.

Troubleshooting checklist (frequent failures)
- SSO login fails: ensure new hire registered authenticator; run `auth-tool verify --user <email>` and check error codes. If `ERR_MFA_NOT_ENROLLED`, instruct to register via SSO URL; if `ERR_USER_NOT_FOUND` escalate to people-ops.
- Laptop imaging failed: escalate to IT Ops; temporary loaner policy applies (loaner devices available for <= 14 days).
- Badge not programmed: verify employee ID in facility system, then request reissue with Facilities ticket `FAC-ISSUE-BADGE` and tag People-ops.

Automations and CLI snippets
- Pre-provision role and repo access (people-ops):
  `onboard preprovision --email maria@example.com --teams infra,eng --repos team-repo,shared-lib`
- Manager grant pattern (for recurring contractors):
  `access-request create --user contractor@example.com --scopes "repo:team-repo:write" --expires 2025-04-30`

Security & compliance guidance
- All initial accounts are created with time-limited default roles; any permanent elevation requires a documented business case.
- Audit logs for access grants are retained for 365 days.
- Physical badge provisioning must be linked to a signed offer and background check clearance for roles that require secure-zone access.

First-week success signals (manager report)
- New hire completed quickstart and opened their first PR.
- New hire is in calendar and Slack, attended at least 3 team events.
- No unresolved access blockers older than 48 hours.

Appendix A: Access request template (copy into IT portal)
- Requester: <manager-name>
- Employee: <employee-name>
- Start date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Systems required: <list>
- Justification: <short description>
- Expiration: <YYYY-MM-DD or none>

Appendix B: Emergency escalation contacts
- People-ops pager: people-ops@redwood.example.com (watch: 9am-6pm PT)
- IT Ops on-call: it-oncall@redwood.example.com (24/7)
- Security incident inbox: sec-ops@redwood.example.com

Related documentation
- See: /confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/manager-first-90-and-career-mobility-playbook-2026 for manager-facing onboarding rhythms.
- See: /confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/onboarding-toolchain-access-and-career-checkpoints-2025 for toolchain-specific deep dives.

Revision history
- 2024-10-20: First draft created by Marisol Chen.
- 2025-06-18: Revised to add CLI snippets and updated badge SLA (Marisol Chen).
",

  "content_field_names": [
    "content"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_be4b992c9bd941c5942e600ef769f6e4"
}

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_f954519b2b004d20acf952719135340a",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/embedded-onboarding-playbook-for-product-and-platform-teams-2026.json",
    "title": "Embedded Onboarding Playbook for Product and Platform Teams",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Embedded Onboarding Playbook for Product and Platform Teams\",\n  \"space\": \"company-handbook\",\n  \"author\": \"Anika Rao\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"people-ops\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-06-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2027-02-14\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Daniel Kim\",\n    \"Priya Mehta\",\n    \"Javier Morales\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"onboarding\",\n    \"embedded\",\n    \"manager-guide\",\n    \"tools\",\n    \"roles\",\n    \"checklist\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"company-handbook/05_internal-tools/onboarding-toolchain-access-and-career-checkpoints-2025\",\n    \"company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/competency-maps-and-rotation-paths-2027\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"body\": \"Overview:\\\\n\\\\nPurpose\\\\nThis playbook defines a repeatable, lightweight embedded onboarding pattern tailored for hires joining Product and Platform teams at Redwood. It aligns role ramp expectations, tooling access timelines, manager and mentor responsibilities, and a standardized handover template so new joiners reach measurable impact faster while minimizing operational friction.\\\\n\\\\nScope\\\\n- Applies to full-time ICs (levels IC1\\u2013IC5) and engineering managers joining Product, Platform, and Core infra teams.\\\\n- Not a replacement for team-specific PRDs or technical deep dives; it supplements those with operational and people processes.\\\\n\\\\nOwners and Escalation\\\\n- Playbook owner: People Ops (Anika Rao).\\\\n- Tier 1 operational owner for tooling: Platform Operations (SRE) team.\\\\n- Escalation: raise to People Ops if provisioning SLAs exceed thresholds (see Access SLA section).\\\\n\\\\nPrinciples\\\\n1) Predictable first 30 days: reduce variability across teams with a 0\\u201330 day milestone map.\\\\n2) Role-tailored but consistent: core checkpoints are uniform; technical ramp content varies by team.\\\\n3) Manager-driven outcomes, mentor-supported development: managers set goals; mentors help reduce cognitive overhead.\\\\n4) Automated, auditable provisioning: avoid ad-hoc access requests.\\\\n\\\\nQuick Start (for hiring manager)\\\\n1. Fill the Embedded Onboarding Form (People Ops template) at offer acceptance.\\\\n2. Assign a primary mentor and a technical buddy before Day 0.\\\\n3. Confirm required tool access and sensitive systems with Platform Ops within 48 hours.\\\\n4. Publish the 90-day success criteria in the team\\u2019s workspace.\\\\n\\\\nPreboarding Checklist (to complete before Day 0)\\\\n- Offer paperwork processed and payroll setup confirmed.\\\\n- Laptop chosen and procurement ticket created (include required GPU/VM specs if applicable).\\\\n- Identity (SSO) account created with base groups: contributor, slack, okta.\\\\n- Read-ahead packet sent (team charter, current roadmap, recent design reviews).\\\\n- First-week calendar blocks created: 1:1s, team orientation, mentor syncs.\\\\n\\\\nDay 0\\u20131: Immediate Priorities\\\\n- 1:1 with manager (goal-setting and success criteria).\\\\n- Intro to mentor and buddy: schedule recurring check-ins (2x/week first month).\\\\n- Verify basic access (email, Slack, docs, code repo read).\\\\n- Run start script: redwood-setup onboard --confirm (see Examples).\\\\n\\\\nWeek 1\\u20132: Build Context and Triage Access\\\\n- Complete team architecture walkthrough and architecture docs.\\\\n- Shadow a deployment/release and an on-call rotation (platform hires).\\\\n- Confirm additional service-specific access (service accounts, deploy keys).\\\\n- Deliverable: short note in team channel summarizing understanding and questions.\\\\n\\\\nWeeks 3\\u20138: First Scoped Deliverable\\\\n- Owner and manager agree a scoped ticket that can land in 2\\u20134 weeks.\\\\n- Weekly progress updates in the team\\u2019s sprint channel.\\\\n- Mentor assists with PR/CR reviews to speed feedback loop.\\\\n\\\\n90-Day Outcomes (expected)\\\\n- New hire has delivered at least one scoped change and conducted a knowledge share.\\\\n- Manager has documented performance and learning plan for next 90 days.\\\\n- People Ops closes onboarding loop and records completion.\\\\n\\\\nRole-Specific Orientation (high level)\\\\n- Product Engineers: focus first week on product metrics, user flows, A/B test signals, and feature flags.\\\\n- Platform Engineers: focus first week on CI/CD pipelines, infra dashboards, incident runbooks, and capacity controls.\\\\n- Product Managers joining engineering teams: ramp on metrics, release cadence, and Git workflow for PRs and specs.\\\\n\\\\nManager Responsibilities (checklist)\\\\n- Provide 90-day success criteria in writing by Day 1.\\\\n- Allocate a mentor and schedule recurring check-ins.\\\\n- Create a scoped deliverable and acceptance criteria by the end of Week 2.\\\\n- Ensure access requests are filed within first 48 hours and follow up to meet SLAs.\\\\n\\\\nMentor/Buddy Responsibilities\\\\n- First two weeks: daily ad-hoc availability and twice-weekly structured syncs.\\\\n- Review first three PRs within 48 hours.\\\\n- Facilitate introductions to core collaborators.\\\\n\\\\nTools & Access Matrix (example)\\\\n| System | Base Access (Day 0\\u20131) | Role-Specific Access | Owner | SLA |\\\\n|--------|-----------------------|----------------------|-------|-----|\\\\n| Slack | Member | N/A | People Ops | 0\\u20131 day |\\\\n| Confluence/docs | Read | Write (after training) | People Ops | 0\\u20131 day |\\\\n| Git (repos) | Read on team repos | Write on assigned repos | Eng DevEx | 0\\u20132 days |\\\\n| CI/CD (deploy) | No | Approve/Deploy for platform | Platform Ops | 2\\u20137 days |\\\\n| Cloud console (prod) | No | IAM role-based access | Cloud Infra | 2\\u201310 days |\\\\n| Monitoring/Dashboards | View | Alerting edit after training | SRE | 1\\u20135 days |\\\\n\\\\nAccess SLA and Request Process\\\\n- Standard SLA targets:\\\\n  - Base access (email, Slack, docs): 24 hours.\\\\n  - Repository write and monitoring view: 48\\u201372 hours.\\\\n  - Production console or service accounts: up to 10 business days (require approval).\\\\n- To request access: file ticket in Platform Ops queue with template: subject \\\\\\\"Access request: <name> \\u2014 <system>\\\\\\\" and include manager approval.\\\\n- Escalation path: after SLA misses of 48 hours for base access, People Ops will intervene.\\\\n\\\\nHandover and Knowledge Transfer Standards\\\\n- All handovers must include: short context paragraph, why change matters, architectural pointers, test coverage notes, and rollback steps.\\\\n- Use the team\\u2019s Handover Template (copyable from People Ops) and include at least one short demo recording (5\\u201310 minutes).\\\\n\\\\nHandover Template (pasteable)\\\\n1. Title and owner\\\\n2. Brief description and business impact\\\\n3. Key services and repos\\\\n4. Runbook excerpt and common failure modes\\\\n5. How to validate a successful change\\\\n6. Contacts and escalation path\\\\n\\\\nExamples and CLI snippets\\\\n- Example: quick local setup (developer machine):\\\\n  1) git clone git@github.com:redwood/<team-repo>.git\\\\n  2) ./scripts/setup-dev.sh --minimal\\\\n  3) export REDWOOD_ENV=dev && ./bin/start-local\\\\n- Example: access bootstrap (internal CLI):\\\\n  $ redwood-iam request --user anika@redwood.com --role repo-write --reason \\\\\\\"onboarding product team\\\\\\\"\\\\n  # check status\\\\n  $ redwood-iam status --request-id RQ-12345\\\\n\\\\nMeasurement and Feedback\\\\n- People Ops will run a 30-day survey to measure ramp clarity, tool access friction, and mentor effectiveness.\\\\n- Key metrics: time-to-first-merge, time-to-deploy, Days-to-base-access (median).\\\\n- Quarterly retro: managers and mentors meet to refine the embedded onboarding checklist.\\\\n\\\\nCommon Pitfalls and Mitigations\\\\n- Pitfall: missing service accounts delaying development. Mitigation: copy standard service-account request during preboarding.\\\\n- Pitfall: overloaded mentors. Mitigation: cap active mentees to 2 per mentor and use rotation windows.\\\\n\\\\nAppendix A \\u2014 Template: 90-Day Success Criteria (example)\\\\n- Objective: Complete a cross-team bug fix that traverses frontend, backend, and infra validation and ship with documentation.\\\\n- Success metrics: PR merged, automated tests green, deployment to staging, and a short knowledge share recorded.\\\\n\\\\nAppendix B \\u2014 Suggested Onboarding Reading List\\\\n- Team README and architecture map\\\\n- Last three release notes and postmortems\\\\n- API contracts and SLOs for services you will own\\\\n\\\\nFrequently Asked Questions\\\\nQ: Who signs off when accesses are delayed?\\\\nA: The hiring manager and People Ops. For production-level access, Cloud Infra approval is required.\\\\n\\\\nQ: Can a mentor be from a different team?\\\\nA: Yes \\u2014 cross-team mentors are encouraged if they reduce context-switching and are familiar with the core tech stack.\\\\n\\\\nRelated resources\\\\n- People Ops: onboarding form and templates\\\\n- Platform Ops: access request flow and SLAs\\\\n- Team workspace: add the new hire to the team\\u2019s onboarding page\\\\n\\\\nLast review notes\\\\n- 2027-02-14: Updated access SLA targets and added example CLI commands.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Embedded Onboarding Playbook for Product and Platform Teams\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/embedded-onboarding-playbook-for-product-and-platform-teams-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: company-handbook\n\nbody : overview : \\ n \\ npurpose \\ nthis playbook defines a repeatable, lightweight embedded onboarding pattern tailored for hires joining product and platform teams at redwood. it aligns role ramp expectations, tooling access timelines, manager and mentor responsibilities, and a standardized handover template so new joiners reach measurable impact faster while minimizing operational friction. \\ n \\ nscope \\ n - applies to full - time ics ( levels ic1 – ic5 ) and engineering managers joining product, platform, and core infra teams. \\ n - not a replacement for team - specific prds or technical deep dives ; it supplements those with operational and people processes. \\ n \\ nowners and escalation \\ n - playbook owner : people ops ( anika rao",

document.title: Embedded Onboarding Playbook for Product and Platform Teams
document.content:
{
  "title": "Embedded Onboarding Playbook for Product and Platform Teams",
  "space": "company-handbook",
  "author": "Anika Rao",
  "owner_team": "people-ops",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-06-15",
  "last_updated": "2027-02-14",
  "reviewers": [
    "Daniel Kim",
    "Priya Mehta",
    "Javier Morales"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "onboarding",
    "embedded",
    "manager-guide",
    "tools",
    "roles",
    "checklist"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "company-handbook/05_internal-tools/onboarding-toolchain-access-and-career-checkpoints-2025",
    "company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/competency-maps-and-rotation-paths-2027"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "Overview:\\n\\nPurpose\\nThis playbook defines a repeatable, lightweight embedded onboarding pattern tailored for hires joining Product and Platform teams at Redwood. It aligns role ramp expectations, tooling access timelines, manager and mentor responsibilities, and a standardized handover template so new joiners reach measurable impact faster while minimizing operational friction.\\n\\nScope\\n- Applies to full-time ICs (levels IC1\u2013IC5) and engineering managers joining Product, Platform, and Core infra teams.\\n- Not a replacement for team-specific PRDs or technical deep dives; it supplements those with operational and people processes.\\n\\nOwners and Escalation\\n- Playbook owner: People Ops (Anika Rao).\\n- Tier 1 operational owner for tooling: Platform Operations (SRE) team.\\n- Escalation: raise to People Ops if provisioning SLAs exceed thresholds (see Access SLA section).\\n\\nPrinciples\\n1) Predictable first 30 days: reduce variability across teams with a 0\u201330 day milestone map.\\n2) Role-tailored but consistent: core checkpoints are uniform; technical ramp content varies by team.\\n3) Manager-driven outcomes, mentor-supported development: managers set goals; mentors help reduce cognitive overhead.\\n4) Automated, auditable provisioning: avoid ad-hoc access requests.\\n\\nQuick Start (for hiring manager)\\n1. Fill the Embedded Onboarding Form (People Ops template) at offer acceptance.\\n2. Assign a primary mentor and a technical buddy before Day 0.\\n3. Confirm required tool access and sensitive systems with Platform Ops within 48 hours.\\n4. Publish the 90-day success criteria in the team\u2019s workspace.\\n\\nPreboarding Checklist (to complete before Day 0)\\n- Offer paperwork processed and payroll setup confirmed.\\n- Laptop chosen and procurement ticket created (include required GPU/VM specs if applicable).\\n- Identity (SSO) account created with base groups: contributor, slack, okta.\\n- Read-ahead packet sent (team charter, current roadmap, recent design reviews).\\n- First-week calendar blocks created: 1:1s, team orientation, mentor syncs.\\n\\nDay 0\u20131: Immediate Priorities\\n- 1:1 with manager (goal-setting and success criteria).\\n- Intro to mentor and buddy: schedule recurring check-ins (2x/week first month).\\n- Verify basic access (email, Slack, docs, code repo read).\\n- Run start script: redwood-setup onboard --confirm (see Examples).\\n\\nWeek 1\u20132: Build Context and Triage Access\\n- Complete team architecture walkthrough and architecture docs.\\n- Shadow a deployment/release and an on-call rotation (platform hires).\\n- Confirm additional service-specific access (service accounts, deploy keys).\\n- Deliverable: short note in team channel summarizing understanding and questions.\\n\\nWeeks 3\u20138: First Scoped Deliverable\\n- Owner and manager agree a scoped ticket that can land in 2\u20134 weeks.\\n- Weekly progress updates in the team\u2019s sprint channel.\\n- Mentor assists with PR/CR reviews to speed feedback loop.\\n\\n90-Day Outcomes (expected)\\n- New hire has delivered at least one scoped change and conducted a knowledge share.\\n- Manager has documented performance and learning plan for next 90 days.\\n- People Ops closes onboarding loop and records completion.\\n\\nRole-Specific Orientation (high level)\\n- Product Engineers: focus first week on product metrics, user flows, A/B test signals, and feature flags.\\n- Platform Engineers: focus first week on CI/CD pipelines, infra dashboards, incident runbooks, and capacity controls.\\n- Product Managers joining engineering teams: ramp on metrics, release cadence, and Git workflow for PRs and specs.\\n\\nManager Responsibilities (checklist)\\n- Provide 90-day success criteria in writing by Day 1.\\n- Allocate a mentor and schedule recurring check-ins.\\n- Create a scoped deliverable and acceptance criteria by the end of Week 2.\\n- Ensure access requests are filed within first 48 hours and follow up to meet SLAs.\\n\\nMentor/Buddy Responsibilities\\n- First two weeks: daily ad-hoc availability and twice-weekly structured syncs.\\n- Review first three PRs within 48 hours.\\n- Facilitate introductions to core collaborators.\\n\\nTools & Access Matrix (example)\\n| System | Base Access (Day 0\u20131) | Role-Specific Access | Owner | SLA |\\n|--------|-----------------------|----------------------|-------|-----|\\n| Slack | Member | N/A | People Ops | 0\u20131 day |\\n| Confluence/docs | Read | Write (after training) | People Ops | 0\u20131 day |\\n| Git (repos) | Read on team repos | Write on assigned repos | Eng DevEx | 0\u20132 days |\\n| CI/CD (deploy) | No | Approve/Deploy for platform | Platform Ops | 2\u20137 days |\\n| Cloud console (prod) | No | IAM role-based access | Cloud Infra | 2\u201310 days |\\n| Monitoring/Dashboards | View | Alerting edit after training | SRE | 1\u20135 days |\\n\\nAccess SLA and Request Process\\n- Standard SLA targets:\\n  - Base access (email, Slack, docs): 24 hours.\\n  - Repository write and monitoring view: 48\u201372 hours.\\n  - Production console or service accounts: up to 10 business days (require approval).\\n- To request access: file ticket in Platform Ops queue with template: subject \\\"Access request: <name> \u2014 <system>\\\" and include manager approval.\\n- Escalation path: after SLA misses of 48 hours for base access, People Ops will intervene.\\n\\nHandover and Knowledge Transfer Standards\\n- All handovers must include: short context paragraph, why change matters, architectural pointers, test coverage notes, and rollback steps.\\n- Use the team\u2019s Handover Template (copyable from People Ops) and include at least one short demo recording (5\u201310 minutes).\\n\\nHandover Template (pasteable)\\n1. Title and owner\\n2. Brief description and business impact\\n3. Key services and repos\\n4. Runbook excerpt and common failure modes\\n5. How to validate a successful change\\n6. Contacts and escalation path\\n\\nExamples and CLI snippets\\n- Example: quick local setup (developer machine):\\n  1) git clone git@github.com:redwood/<team-repo>.git\\n  2) ./scripts/setup-dev.sh --minimal\\n  3) export REDWOOD_ENV=dev && ./bin/start-local\\n- Example: access bootstrap (internal CLI):\\n  $ redwood-iam request --user anika@redwood.com --role repo-write --reason \\\"onboarding product team\\\"\\n  # check status\\n  $ redwood-iam status --request-id RQ-12345\\n\\nMeasurement and Feedback\\n- People Ops will run a 30-day survey to measure ramp clarity, tool access friction, and mentor effectiveness.\\n- Key metrics: time-to-first-merge, time-to-deploy, Days-to-base-access (median).\\n- Quarterly retro: managers and mentors meet to refine the embedded onboarding checklist.\\n\\nCommon Pitfalls and Mitigations\\n- Pitfall: missing service accounts delaying development. Mitigation: copy standard service-account request during preboarding.\\n- Pitfall: overloaded mentors. Mitigation: cap active mentees to 2 per mentor and use rotation windows.\\n\\nAppendix A \u2014 Template: 90-Day Success Criteria (example)\\n- Objective: Complete a cross-team bug fix that traverses frontend, backend, and infra validation and ship with documentation.\\n- Success metrics: PR merged, automated tests green, deployment to staging, and a short knowledge share recorded.\\n\\nAppendix B \u2014 Suggested Onboarding Reading List\\n- Team README and architecture map\\n- Last three release notes and postmortems\\n- API contracts and SLOs for services you will own\\n\\nFrequently Asked Questions\\nQ: Who signs off when accesses are delayed?\\nA: The hiring manager and People Ops. For production-level access, Cloud Infra approval is required.\\n\\nQ: Can a mentor be from a different team?\\nA: Yes \u2014 cross-team mentors are encouraged if they reduce context-switching and are familiar with the core tech stack.\\n\\nRelated resources\\n- People Ops: onboarding form and templates\\n- Platform Ops: access request flow and SLAs\\n- Team workspace: add the new hire to the team\u2019s onboarding page\\n\\nLast review notes\\n- 2027-02-14: Updated access SLA targets and added example CLI commands. (Anika Rao)\\n\\nContact\\nPeople Ops (onboarding): onboarding@redwood.com\\nPlatform Ops (access requests): platform-ops@redwood.com\\n",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "body"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_f954519b2b004d20acf952719135340a"
}

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"IC first-90 operating rhythm and tool access\",\n  \"space\": \"company-handbook\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Kapoor\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"people-ops\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-01\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-06-15\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Marco Li\",\n    \"Sofia Reynolds\",\n    \"Diego Alvarez\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"individual-contributor\",\n    \"onboarding\",\n    \"first-90\",\n    \"tools\",\n    \"career-path\",\n    \"operating-rhythm\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/competency-maps-and-rotation-paths-2027\",\n    \"/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/new-hire-orientation-and-tooling-guide-2024\",\n    \"/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"body\": \"Overview\\n\\nPurpose: This guide is a practical, role-agnostic first-90 playbook for Individual Contributors (ICs) joining Redwood. It combines an operating rhythm (meetings, checkpoints, and progress markers) with the exact tool and account access checklist that new ICs need to be productive day one through day 90.\\n\\nScope: Applicable to ICs across engineering, product, research, and platform teams. Managers should adapt milestones to team-specific objectives and share the plan during the first 1:1. People Ops owns the baseline checklist and account provisioning timelines.\\n\\nOutcomes (by day 90)\\n- Full access to required tooling and repositories with documented troubleshooting notes.\\n- Clear set of deliverables for first quarter: at least one deliverable with measurable outcome (bugfix, small feature, doc, or instrumentation item).\\n- Career-aligned growth conversation: manager and IC agree on 90-day impact and a visible development plan.\\n- Integration into team operating cadence with regular contributions to standups, planning, and retros.\\n\\nQuick start timeline (high level)\\n1) Day 0\\u20133: Orientation and core access\\n   - Complete People Ops orientation and submit equipment confirmation form.\\n   - Confirm SSO/MFA, VPN, and device enrollment.\\n   - Join primary team Slack channels, PagerDuty (if oncall), and calendar invites for team ceremonies.\\n2) Week 1: Foundations and context\\n   - Read team readmes, architecture overview, and key RFCs.\\n   - Shadow pair session and small starter ticket assigned.\\n   - Complete security and data-handling training modules.\\n3) Weeks 2\\u20134: Contribution and feedback loops\\n   - Ship first small change (doc, test, pipeline fix, or low-risk code).\\n   - 30-day sync: review blockers, update onboarding checklist, and refine goals.\\n4) Month 2: Ownership and expansion\\n   - Take ownership of a small area (test suite, dashboard, or routine infra task).\\n   - Start a retrospective-style write-up of early observations and suggested improvements for the area.\\n5) Month 3: Impact and career planning\\n   - Deliver primary 90-day milestone.\\n   - 90-day review: calibration with manager; update development plan and recommended learning milestones.\\n\\nDetailed tool/account access checklist (baseline)\\n- Identity & Security\\n  - SSO (Okta): account provisioned and MFA configured.\\n  - Device enrollment (MDM): macOS/Linux/Windows enrollment complete.\\n  - KMS access requests started for encryption/materials if applicable.\\n- Communication & Calendar\\n  - Slack: added to team/private channels and core global channels (announcements, all-hands).\\n  - Google Workspace: mailbox, calendar, Drive, and shared team drives.\\n- Code & CI/CD\\n  - GitHub: org membership, repo-level write access (or CLA process started), branch protection notes.\\n  - CI: build status notification in Slack for core repos.\\n  - Container registry access (where relevant).\\n- Cloud & Infra\\n  - GCP/AWS account with IAM role scoped to environment (dev/staging).\\n  - Console access gated behind approval; temporary elevated access process documented.\\n  - Secrets manager (Vault/Secrets Manager) read access requested for dev environment.\\n- Observability & Incidents\\n  - Grafana/Datadog: read access and saved dashboards added to favorites.\\n  - Logging: index and search training for service-level logs.\\n  - PagerDuty: oncall training and escalation steps if included on rotation.\\n- Product & Design Tools\\n  - Figma, Miro, and product analytics dashboards (Amplitude/Looker) as applicable.\\n- Internal Knowledge & Docs\\n  - Confluence: access to team pages, architecture decisions, and onboarding playbooks.\\n  - Shared templates: PR templates, runbook templates, and RFC template.\\n\\nMinimum SLAs for provisioning (People Ops commitments)\\n| Item | Target | Owner | Notes |\\n|-------|--------|-------|-------|\\n| Okta + MDM | 24 hours | People Ops | Push reminder if delayed after 48h |\\n| GitHub org invite | 48 hours | Engineering Ops | Repo-specific access may take longer (team leads) |\\n| Cloud dev role | 72 hours | Infra | Approvals required for sensitive services |\\n| PagerDuty invite | 48 hours | Eng SRE | Oncall training must be scheduled before rotation |\\n\\nFirst-90 operating rhythm (example week cadence)\\n- Weekly\\n  - Team standup (15min): status updates and blockers.\\n  - 1:1 with manager (30\\u201345min): coaching, blockers, and development.\\n  - Office hours with buddy/mentor (1hr): pairing and Q&A.\\n- Biweekly\\n  - Sprint planning / backlog refinement (60\\u201390min).\\n  - Cross-functional sync (product + design) for active projects (30\\u201360min).\\n- Monthly\\n  - Team retro and metrics review (90min): shape improvement actions.\\n  - Engineering brown bag / knowledge share (45\\u201360min).\\n- End of quarter\\n  - 90-day review and objective calibration (manager + IC).\\n\\nRole-specific onboarding addenda (short list)\\n- Software Engineers: local dev environment template, test harness walkthrough, and performance budget doc.\\n- MLEs / Applied ML: model sandbox access, evaluation harness, and dataset S3/GCS roles.\\n- Product: customer journey dashboards, feature flags overview, and release gate checklist.\\n- SRE/Infra: runbook library, service ownership matrix, and CI runner access.\\n\\nManager checklist for first-90 (quick reference)\\n1. Share team mission, immediate priorities, and success metrics within first 3 days.\\n2. Assign a buddy and schedule daily check-ins for week 1.\\n3. Ensure required access tickets are created and tracked (link to provisioning tracker).\\n4. Set an initial 30/60/90 goal sheet with measurable outcomes and examples of success.\\n5. Provide early feedback and document decisions in Confluence.\\n\\nHandover and documentation expectations (IC responsibility)\\n- Create a short \\\"What I worked on\\\" doc for each shipped item with: problem statement, design decisions, tests added, and rollbacks.\\n- Maintain or update at least one runbook/RFC within first 90 days.\\n- Add onboarding notes to team wiki covering any setup gotchas encountered.\\n\\nCommon provisioning failure modes and remediation (troubleshooting)\\n- Missing Okta group mapping: escalate to People Ops with screenshot and employee ID.\\n- GitHub invite expired: engineering-ops can reissue invites; confirm email alias.\\n- Cloud role blocked by billing policy: Infra requires a cost-owner approval; attach request ticket.\\n- PagerDuty not receiving notifications: check DO NOT DISTURB settings and verify phone/SMS on file.\\n\\nTemplates and artifacts (quick links)\\n- 30/60/90 goal template (copyable): /confluence/templates/ic-30-60-90\\n- PR checklist and release checklist: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs/pr-and-release-checklists\\n- Runbook template: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/templates\\n\\nFAQ (short)\\nQ: I don\\u2019t have access to a repo I need. What do I do?\\nA: File an access request in the provisioning tracker, message your manager and ping engineering-ops. If it\\u2019s blocking Day 1 work, mark the ticket as high priority.\\n\\nQ: Who signs off the 90-day milestone?\\nA: The manager signs off the milestone after a documented demo and discussion; calibration with team lead or product partner may be requested for scope alignment.\\n\\nAppendix: example 30/60/90 goal sheet (text)\\n- 30-day goals:\\n  - Complete local dev setup and ship a documentation fix.\\n  - Demonstrate ability to run the test suite and debug a failing CI job.\\n- 60-day goals:\\n  - Own a minor feature or stabilization task end-to-end; collect user/metric feedback.\\n  - Present a 15-minute learning summary to the team.\\n- 90-day goals:\\n  - Deliver primary milestone described during onboarding and propose one improvement to the team\\u2019s operating model.\\n\\nContact & ownership\\n- People Ops onboarding lead: people-ops@redwood.ai\\n- Engineering Ops: eng-ops@redwood.ai\\n- Platform & Infra request queue: infra-requests@redwood.ai\\n\\nChange log\\n- 2026-02-01: Created by Aisha Kapoor (People Ops baseline).\\n- 2026-03-20: Added cloud provisioning SLA table and role-specific addenda (reviewed by Marco Li).\\n- 2026-06-15: Updated templates links and clarified PagerDuty onboarding steps (reviewed by Sofia Reynolds).\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_dbbeebb87274453e85f5abb97544c508\"\n}",

{
  "title": "IC first-90 operating rhythm and tool access",
  "space": "company-handbook",
  "author": "Aisha Kapoor",
  "owner_team": "people-ops",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-02-01",
  "last_updated": "2026-06-15",
  "reviewers": [
    "Marco Li",
    "Sofia Reynolds",
    "Diego Alvarez"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "individual-contributor",
    "onboarding",
    "first-90",
    "tools",
    "career-path",
    "operating-rhythm"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/competency-maps-and-rotation-paths-2027",
    "/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/new-hire-orientation-and-tooling-guide-2024",
    "/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "Overview

Purpose: This guide is a practical, role-agnostic first-90 playbook for Individual Contributors (ICs) joining Redwood. It combines an operating rhythm (meetings, checkpoints, and progress markers) with the exact tool and account access checklist that new ICs need to be productive day one through day 90.

Scope: Applicable to ICs across engineering, product, research, and platform teams. Managers should adapt milestones to team-specific objectives and share the plan during the first 1:1. People Ops owns the baseline checklist and account provisioning timelines.

Outcomes (by day 90)
- Full access to required tooling and repositories with documented troubleshooting notes.
- Clear set of deliverables for first quarter: at least one deliverable with measurable outcome (bugfix, small feature, doc, or instrumentation item).
- Career-aligned growth conversation: manager and IC agree on 90-day impact and a visible development plan.
- Integration into team operating cadence with regular contributions to standups, planning, and retros.

Quick start timeline (high level)
1) Day 0–3: Orientation and core access
   - Complete People Ops orientation and submit equipment confirmation form.
   - Confirm SSO/MFA, VPN, and device enrollment.
   - Join primary team Slack channels, PagerDuty (if oncall), and calendar invites for team ceremonies.
2) Week 1: Foundations and context
   - Read team readmes, architecture overview, and key RFCs.
   - Shadow pair session and small starter ticket assigned.
   - Complete security and data-handling training modules.
3) Weeks 2–4: Contribution and feedback loops
   - Ship first small change (doc, test, pipeline fix, or low-risk code).
   - 30-day sync: review blockers, update onboarding checklist, and refine goals.
4) Month 2: Ownership and expansion
   - Take ownership of a small area (test suite, dashboard, or routine infra task).
   - Start a retrospective-style write-up of early observations and suggested improvements for the area.
5) Month 3: Impact and career planning
   - Deliver primary 90-day milestone.
   - 90-day review: calibration with manager; update development plan and recommended learning milestones.

Detailed tool/account access checklist (baseline)
- Identity & Security
  - SSO (Okta): account provisioned and MFA configured.
  - Device enrollment (MDM): macOS/Linux/Windows enrollment complete.
  - KMS access requests started for encryption/materials if applicable.
- Communication & Calendar
  - Slack: added to team/private channels and core global channels (announcements, all-hands).
  - Google Workspace: mailbox, calendar, Drive, and shared team drives.
- Code & CI/CD
  - GitHub: org membership, repo-level write access (or CLA process started), branch protection notes.
  - CI: build status notification in Slack for core repos.
  - Container registry access (where relevant).
- Cloud & Infra
  - GCP/AWS account with IAM role scoped to environment (dev/staging).
  - Console access gated behind approval; temporary elevated access process documented.
  - Secrets manager (Vault/Secrets Manager) read access requested for dev environment.
- Observability & Incidents
  - Grafana/Datadog: read access and saved dashboards added to favorites.
  - Logging: index and search training for service-level logs.
  - PagerDuty: oncall training and escalation steps if included on rotation.
- Product & Design Tools
  - Figma, Miro, and product analytics dashboards (Amplitude/Looker) as applicable.
- Internal Knowledge & Docs
  - Confluence: access to team pages, architecture decisions, and onboarding playbooks.
  - Shared templates: PR templates, runbook templates, and RFC template.

Minimum SLAs for provisioning (People Ops commitments)
| Item | Target | Owner | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|-------|
| Okta + MDM | 24 hours | People Ops | Push reminder if delayed after 48h |
| GitHub org invite | 48 hours | Engineering Ops | Repo-specific access may take longer (team leads) |
| Cloud dev role | 72 hours | Infra | Approvals required for sensitive services |
| PagerDuty invite | 48 hours | Eng SRE | Oncall training must be scheduled before rotation |

First-90 operating rhythm (example week cadence)
- Weekly
  - Team standup (15min): status updates and blockers.
  - 1:1 with manager (30–45min): coaching, blockers, and development.
  - Office hours with buddy/mentor (1hr): pairing and Q&A.
- Biweekly
  - Sprint planning / backlog refinement (60–90min).
  - Cross-functional sync (product + design) for active projects (30–60min).
- Monthly
  - Team retro and metrics review (90min): shape improvement actions.
  - Engineering brown bag / knowledge share (45–60min).
- End of quarter
  - 90-day review and objective calibration (manager + IC).

Role-specific onboarding addenda (short list)
- Software Engineers: local dev environment template, test harness walkthrough, and performance budget doc.
- MLEs / Applied ML: model sandbox access, evaluation harness, and dataset S3/GCS roles.
- Product: customer journey dashboards, feature flags overview, and release gate checklist.
- SRE/Infra: runbook library, service ownership matrix, and CI runner access.

Manager checklist for first-90 (quick reference)
1. Share team mission, immediate priorities, and success metrics within first 3 days.
2. Assign a buddy and schedule daily check-ins for week 1.
3. Ensure required access tickets are created and tracked (link to provisioning tracker).
4. Set an initial 30/60/90 goal sheet with measurable outcomes and examples of success.
5. Provide early feedback and document decisions in Confluence.

Handover and documentation expectations (IC responsibility)
- Create a short "What I worked on" doc for each shipped item with: problem statement, design decisions, tests added, and rollbacks.
- Maintain or update at least one runbook/RFC within first 90 days.
- Add onboarding notes to team wiki covering any setup gotchas encountered.

Common provisioning failure modes and remediation (troubleshooting)
- Missing Okta group mapping: escalate to People Ops with screenshot and employee ID.
- GitHub invite expired: engineering-ops can reissue invites; confirm email alias.
- Cloud role blocked by billing policy: Infra requires a cost-owner approval; attach request ticket.
- PagerDuty not receiving notifications: check DO NOT DISTURB settings and verify phone/SMS on file.

Templates and artifacts (quick links)
- 30/60/90 goal template (copyable): /confluence/templates/ic-30-60-90
- PR checklist and release checklist: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs/pr-and-release-checklists
- Runbook template: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/templates

FAQ (short)
Q: I don’t have access to a repo I need. What do I do?
A: File an access request in the provisioning tracker, message your manager and ping engineering-ops. If it’s blocking Day 1 work, mark the ticket as high priority.

Q: Who signs off the 90-day milestone?
A: The manager signs off the milestone after a documented demo and discussion; calibration with team lead or product partner may be requested for scope alignment.

Appendix: example 30/60/90 goal sheet (text)
- 30-day goals:
  - Complete local dev setup and ship a documentation fix.
  - Demonstrate ability to run the test suite and debug a failing CI job.
- 60-day goals:
  - Own a minor feature or stabilization task end-to-end; collect user/metric feedback.
  - Present a 15-minute learning summary to the team.
- 90-day goals:
  - Deliver primary milestone described during onboarding and propose one improvement to the team’s operating model.

Contact & ownership
- People Ops onboarding lead: people-ops@redwood.ai
- Engineering Ops: eng-ops@redwood.ai
- Platform & Infra request queue: infra-requests@redwood.ai

Change log
- 2026-02-01: Created by Aisha Kapoor (People Ops baseline).
- 2026-03-20: Added cloud provisioning SLA table and role-specific addenda (reviewed by Marco Li).
- 2026-06-15: Updated templates links and clarified PagerDuty onboarding steps (reviewed by Sofia Reynolds).",

{
  "document": {
    "id": "enterprise_b9e03890a22cfc276b5468d4",
    "path": "/code/litellm/CONTRIBUTING.md",
    "title": "litellm: CONTRIBUTING.md",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/codebase/litellm",
    "content": "# Contributing to LiteLLM\n\nThank you for your interest in contributing to LiteLLM! We welcome contributions of all kinds - from bug fixes and documentation improvements to new features and integrations.\n\n## **Checklist before submitting a PR**\n\nHere are the core requirements for any PR submitted to LiteLLM:\n\n- [ ] **Sign the Contributor License Agreement (CLA)** - [see details](#contributor-license-agreement-cla)\n- [ ] **Keep scope isolated** - Your changes should address 1 specific problem at a time\n\n#### Proxy (Backend) PRs\n\n- [ ] **Add testing** - Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement - [see details](#adding-testing)\n- [ ] **Ensure your PR passes all checks**:\n  - [ ] [Unit Tests](#running-unit-tests) - `make test-unit`\n  - [ ] [Linting / Formatting](#running-linting-and-formatting-checks) - `make lint`\n\n#### UI PRs\n\n- [ ] **Ensure the UI builds successfully** - `npm run build`\n- [ ] **Ensure all UI unit tests pass** - `npm run test`\n- [ ] **Add tests for new components or logic** - If you are adding a new component or new logic, add corresponding tests\n\n## **Contributor License Agreement (CLA)**\n\nBefore contributing code to LiteLLM, you must sign our [Contributor License Agreement (CLA)](https://cla-assistant.io/BerriAI/litellm). This is a legal requirement for all contributions to be merged into the main repository.\n\n**Important:** We strongly recommend reviewing and signing the CLA before starting work on your contribution to avoid any delays in the PR process.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### 1. Setup Your Local Development Environment\n\n```bash\n# Fork the repository on GitHub (click the Fork button at https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm)\n# Then clone your fork locally\ngit clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/litellm.git\ncd litellm\n\n# Create a new branch for your feature (see \"Commit and Branch Conventions\" below)\ngit checkout -b feature/your-feature\n\n# Install development dependencies\nmake install-dev\n\n# Install git hooks that enforce commit + branch conventions (one-time, opt-in)\nmake install-hooks\n\n# Verify your setup works\nmake help\n```\n\nThat's it! Your local development environment is ready.\n\n## Commit and Branch Conventions\n\nCommits follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) and branches follow [Conventional Branches](https://conventional-branch.github.io/). Run `make install-hooks` once per clone to enable the local git hooks that enforce these — see the [contributor docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code#commit-and-branch-conventions) for the full type list, examples, the protected-branch bypass list, and how to opt out.\n\n### 2. Development Workflow\n\nHere's the recommended workflow for making changes:\n\n```bash\n# Make your changes to the code\n# ...\n\n# Format your code (auto-fixes formatting issues)\nmake format\n\n# Run all linting checks (matches CI exactly)\nmake lint\n\n# Run unit tests to ensure nothing is broken\nmake test-unit\n\n# Commit your changes (must follow Conventional Commits — see above)\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"feat(scope): your descriptive commit message\"\n\n# Push and create a PR (branch must follow Conventional Branches — see above)\ngit push origin feature/your-feature\n```\n\n## Adding Testing\n\n**Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement for all PRs.**\n\n### Where to Add Tests\n\nAdd your tests to the [`tests/test_litellm/` directory](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm).\n\n- This directory mirrors the structure of the `litellm/` directory\n- **Only add mocked tests** - no real LLM API calls in this directory\n- For integration tests with real APIs, use the appropriate test directories\n\n### File Naming Convention\n\nThe `tests/test_litellm/` directory follows the same structure as `litellm/`:\n\n- `litellm/proxy/caching_routes.py` → `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_caching_routes.py`\n- `litellm/utils.py` → `tests/test_litellm/test_utils.py`\n\n### Example Test\n\n```python\nimport pytest\nfrom litellm import completion\n\ndef test_your_feature():\n    \"\"\"Test your feature with a descriptive docstring.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    messages = [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Hello\"}]\n    \n    # Act\n    # Use mocked responses, not real API calls\n    \n    # Assert\n    assert expected_result == actual_result\n```\n\n## Running Tests and Checks\n\n### Running Unit Tests\n\nRun all unit tests (uses parallel execution for speed):\n\n```bash\nmake test-unit\n```\n\nIf you're running broader test suites, proxy tests, or anything that touches PostgreSQL-backed fixtures/plugins, install the full local test environment first:\n\n```bash\nmake install-test-deps\n```\n\nThis syncs the locked test environment used across the repo, including `psycopg` v3 plus `psycopg-binary` (used by `pytest-postgresql`), `psycopg2-binary` (used by some proxy E2E tests), and a generated Prisma client for DB-backed proxy tests, so pytest startup matches CI without manual package installs.\n\nRun specific test files:\n```bash\nuv run pytest tests/test_litellm/test_your_file.py -v\n```\n\n### Running Linting and Formatting Checks\n\nRun all linting checks (matches CI exactly):\n\n```bash\nmake lint\n```\n\nIndividual linting commands:\n```bash\nmake format-check       # Check Black formatting\nmake lint-ruff          # Run Ruff linting\nmake lint-basedpyright  # Run basedpyright type checking\nmake check-circular-imports    # Check for circular imports\nmake check-import-safety       # Check import safety\n```\n\nApply formatting (auto-fixes issues):\n```bash\nmake format\n```\n\n> **Black formatting is enforced in CI.** All PRs must pass the Black formatting check.\n>\n> - **AI coding agents** (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, etc.): `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` instruct agents to run `poetry run black .` before committing.\n> - **VS Code users**: Install the [Black Formatter extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-python.black-formatter) and enable format-on-save:\n>   ```json\n>   {\n>     \"[python]\": {\n>       \"editor.defaultFormatter\": \"ms-python.black-formatter\",\n>       \"editor.formatOnSave\": true\n>     }\n>   }\n>   ```\n\n### CI Compatibility\n\nTo ensure your changes will pass CI, run the exact same checks locally:\n\n```bash\n# This runs the same checks as the GitHub workflows\nmake lint\nmake test-unit\n```\n\nFor exact CI compatibility (pins OpenAI version like CI):\n```bash\nmake install-dev-ci     # Installs exact CI dependencies\n```\n\n## Available Make Commands\n\nRun `make help` to see all available commands:\n\n```bash\nmake help                       # Show all available commands\nmake install-dev               # Install development dependencies\nmake install-proxy-dev         # Install proxy development dependencies\nmake install-test-deps         # Install the full local test environment\nmake format                    # Apply Black code formatting\nmake format-check              # Check Black formatting (matches CI)\nmake lint                      # Run all linting checks\nmake test-unit                 # Run unit tests\nmake test-integration          # Run integration tests\nmake test-unit-helm            # Run Helm unit tests\n```\n\n## Code Quality Standards\n\nLiteLLM follows the [Google Python Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/pyguide.html).\n\nOur automated quality checks include:\n- **Black** for consistent code formatting\n- **Ruff** for linting and code quality\n- **basedpyright** for static type checking\n- **Circular import detection**\n- **Import safety validation**\n\nAll checks must pass before your PR can be merged.\n\n## Common Issues and Solutions\n\n### 1. Linting Failures\n\nIf `make lint` fails:\n\n1. **Formatting issues**: Run `make format` to auto-fix\n2. **Ruff issues**: Check the output and fix manually\n3. **basedpyright issues**: Add proper type hints\n4. **Circular imports**: Refactor import dependencies\n5. **Import safety**: Fix any unprotected imports\n\n### 2. Test Failures\n\nIf `make test-unit` fails:\n\n1. Check if you broke existing functionality\n2. Add tests for your new code\n3. Ensure tests use mocks, not real API calls\n4. Check test file naming conventions\n\n### 3. Common Development Tips\n\n- **Use type hints**: basedpyright requires proper type annotations\n- **Write descriptive commit messages**: Help reviewers understand your changes\n- **Keep PRs focused**: One feature/fix per PR\n- **Test edge cases**: Don't just test the happy path\n- **Update documentation**: If you change APIs, update docs\n\n## Building and Running Locally\n\n### LiteLLM Proxy Server\n\nTo run the proxy server locally:\n\n```bash\n# Install proxy dependencies\nmake install-proxy-dev\n\n# Start the proxy server\nuv run litellm --config your_config.yaml\n```\n\n### Docker Development\n\nIf you want to build the Docker image yourself:\n\n```bash\n# Build using the non-root Dockerfile\ndocker build -f docker/Dockerfile.non_root -t litellm_dev .\n\n# Run with your config\ndocker run \\\n    -v $(pwd)/proxy_config.yaml:/app/config.yaml \\\n    -e LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=\"sk-1234\" \\\n    -p 4000:4000 \\\n    litellm_dev \\\n    --config /app/config.yaml --detailed_debug\n```\n\n## UI Development\n\n### 1. Setup Your Local UI Development Environment\n\n```bash\n# Clone the repo (if you haven't already)\ngit clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/litellm.git\ncd litellm\n\n# Navigate to the UI dashboard directory\ncd ui/litellm-dashboard\n\n# Install dependencies\nnpm install\n\n# Start the development server\nnpm run dev\n```\n\n### 2. Adding UI Tests\n\nIf you are adding a **new component** or **new logic**, you must add corresponding tests.\n\n### 3. Running UI Unit Tests\n\n```bash\nnpm run test\n```\n\n### 4. Building the UI\n\nEnsure the UI builds successfully before submitting your PR:\n\n```bash\nnpm run build\n```\n\n## Submitting Your PR\n\n1. **Push your branch**: `git push origin your-feature-branch`\n2. **Create a PR**: Go to GitHub and open a pull request against [`litellm_internal_staging`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/litellm_internal_staging), which is the default base branch. Do not target `main`.\n3. **Fill out the PR template**: Provide clear description of changes\n4. **Wait for review**: Maintainers will review and provide feedback\n5. **Address feedback**: Make requested changes and push updates\n6. **Merge**: Once approved, your PR will be merged!\n\n## Getting Help\n\nIf you need help:\n\n- 💬 [Join our Discord](https://discord.gg/wuPM9dRgDw)\n- 💬 [Join our Slack](https://www.litellm.ai/support)\n- 📧 Email us: ishaan@berri.ai / krrish@berri.ai\n- 🐛 [Create an issue](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/new)\n\n## What to Contribute\n\nLooking for ideas? Check out:\n\n- 🐛 [Good first issues](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/labels/good%20first%20issue)\n- 🚀 [Feature requests](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/labels/enhancement)\n- 📚 Documentation improvements\n- 🧪 Test coverage improvements\n- 🔌 New LLM provider integrations\n\nThank you for contributing to LiteLLM! 🚀 \n",

document.content:
# Contributing to LiteLLM

Thank you for your interest in contributing to LiteLLM! We welcome contributions of all kinds - from bug fixes and documentation improvements to new features and integrations.

## **Checklist before submitting a PR**

Here are the core requirements for any PR submitted to LiteLLM:

- [ ] **Sign the Contributor License Agreement (CLA)** - [see details](#contributor-license-agreement-cla)
- [ ] **Keep scope isolated** - Your changes should address 1 specific problem at a time

#### Proxy (Backend) PRs

- [ ] **Add testing** - Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement - [see details](#adding-testing)
- [ ] **Ensure your PR passes all checks**:
  - [ ] [Unit Tests](#running-unit-tests) - `make test-unit`
  - [ ] [Linting / Formatting](#running-linting-and-formatting-checks) - `make lint`

#### UI PRs

- [ ] **Ensure the UI builds successfully** - `npm run build`
- [ ] **Ensure all UI unit tests pass** - `npm run test`
- [ ] **Add tests for new components or logic** - If you are adding a new component or new logic, add corresponding tests

## **Contributor License Agreement (CLA)**

Before contributing code to LiteLLM, you must sign our [Contributor License Agreement (CLA)](https://cla-assistant.io/BerriAI/litellm). This is a legal requirement for all contributions to be merged into the main repository.

**Important:** We strongly recommend reviewing and signing the CLA before starting work on your contribution to avoid any delays in the PR process.

## Quick Start

### 1. Setup Your Local Development Environment

```bash
# Fork the repository on GitHub (click the Fork button at https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm)
# Then clone your fork locally
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/litellm.git
cd litellm

# Create a new branch for your feature (see "Commit and Branch Conventions" below)
git checkout -b feature/your-feature

# Install development dependencies
make install-dev

# Install git hooks that enforce commit + branch conventions (one-time, opt-in)
make install-hooks

# Verify your setup works
make help
```

That's it! Your local development environment is ready.

## Commit and Branch Conventions

Commits follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) and branches follow [Conventional Branches](https://conventional-branch.github.io/). Run `make install-hooks` once per clone to enable the local git hooks that enforce these — see the [contributor docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code#commit-and-branch-conventions) for the full type list, examples, the protected-branch bypass list, and how to opt out.

### 2. Development Workflow

Here's the recommended workflow for making changes:

```bash
# Make your changes to the code
# ...

# Format your code (auto-fixes formatting issues)
make format

# Run all linting checks (matches CI exactly)
make lint

# Run unit tests to ensure nothing is broken
make test-unit

# Commit your changes (must follow Conventional Commits — see above)
git add .
git commit -m "feat(scope): your descriptive commit message"

# Push and create a PR (branch must follow Conventional Branches — see above)
git push origin feature/your-feature
```

## Adding Testing

**Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement for all PRs.**

### Where to Add Tests

Add your tests to the [`tests/test_litellm/` directory](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm).

- This directory mirrors the structure of the `litellm/` directory
- **Only add mocked tests** - no real LLM API calls in this directory
- For integration tests with real APIs, use the appropriate test directories

### File Naming Convention

The `tests/test_litellm/` directory follows the same structure as `litellm/`:

- `litellm/proxy/caching_routes.py` → `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_caching_routes.py`
- `litellm/utils.py` → `tests/test_litellm/test_utils.py`

### Example Test

```python
import pytest
from litellm import completion

def test_your_feature():
    """Test your feature with a descriptive docstring."""
    # Arrange
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
    
    # Act
    # Use mocked responses, not real API calls
    
    # Assert
    assert expected_result == actual_result
```

## Running Tests and Checks

### Running Unit Tests

Run all unit tests (uses parallel execution for speed):

```bash
make test-unit
```

If you're running broader test suites, proxy tests, or anything that touches PostgreSQL-backed fixtures/plugins, install the full local test environment first:

```bash
make install-test-deps
```

This syncs the locked test environment used across the repo, including `psycopg` v3 plus `psycopg-binary` (used by `pytest-postgresql`), `psycopg2-binary` (used by some proxy E2E tests), and a generated Prisma client for DB-backed proxy tests, so pytest startup matches CI without manual package installs.

Run specific test files:
```bash
uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/test_your_file.py -v
```

### Running Linting and Formatting Checks

Run all linting checks (matches CI exactly):

```bash
make lint
```

Individual linting commands:
```bash
make format-check       # Check Black formatting
make lint-ruff          # Run Ruff linting
make lint-basedpyright  # Run basedpyright type checking
make check-circular-imports    # Check for circular imports
make check-import-safety       # Check import safety
```

Apply formatting (auto-fixes issues):
```bash
make format
```

> **Black formatting is enforced in CI.** All PRs must pass the Black formatting check.
>
> - **AI coding agents** (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, etc.): `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` instruct agents to run `poetry run black .` before committing.
> - **VS Code users**: Install the [Black Formatter extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-python.black-formatter) and enable format-on-save:
>   ```json
>   {
>     "[python]": {
>       "editor.defaultFormatter": "ms-python.black-formatter",
>       "editor.formatOnSave": true
>     }
>   }
>   ```

### CI Compatibility

To ensure your changes will pass CI, run the exact same checks locally:

```bash
# This runs the same checks as the GitHub workflows
make lint
make test-unit
```

For exact CI compatibility (pins OpenAI version like CI):
```bash
make install-dev-ci     # Installs exact CI dependencies
```

## Available Make Commands

Run `make help` to see all available commands:

```bash
make help                       # Show all available commands
make install-dev               # Install development dependencies
make install-proxy-dev         # Install proxy development dependencies
make install-test-deps         # Install the full local test environment
make format                    # Apply Black code formatting
make format-check              # Check Black formatting (matches CI)
make lint                      # Run all linting checks
make test-unit                 # Run unit tests
make test-integration          # Run integration tests
make test-unit-helm            # Run Helm unit tests
```

## Code Quality Standards

LiteLLM follows the [Google Python Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/pyguide.html).

Our automated quality checks include:
- **Black** for consistent code formatting
- **Ruff** for linting and code quality
- **basedpyright** for static type checking
- **Circular import detection**
- **Import safety validation**

All checks must pass before your PR can be merged.

## Common Issues and Solutions

### 1. Linting Failures

If `make lint` fails:

1. **Formatting issues**: Run `make format` to auto-fix
2. **Ruff issues**: Check the output and fix manually
3. **basedpyright issues**: Add proper type hints
4. **Circular imports**: Refactor import dependencies
5. **Import safety**: Fix any unprotected imports

### 2. Test Failures

If `make test-unit` fails:

1. Check if you broke existing functionality
2. Add tests for your new code
3. Ensure tests use mocks, not real API calls
4. Check test file naming conventions

### 3. Common Development Tips

- **Use type hints**: basedpyright requires proper type annotations
- **Write descriptive commit messages**: Help reviewers understand your changes
- **Keep PRs focused**: One feature/fix per PR
- **Test edge cases**: Don't just test the happy path
- **Update documentation**: If you change APIs, update docs

## Building and Running Locally

### LiteLLM Proxy Server

To run the proxy server locally:

```bash
# Install proxy dependencies
make install-proxy-dev

# Start the proxy server
uv run litellm --config your_config.yaml
```

### Docker Development

If you want to build the Docker image yourself:

```bash
# Build using the non-root Dockerfile
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile.non_root -t litellm_dev .

# Run with your config
docker run \
    -v $(pwd)/proxy_config.yaml:/app/config.yaml \
    -e LITELLM_MASTER_KEY="sk-1234" \
    -p 4000:4000 \
    litellm_dev \
    --config /app/config.yaml --detailed_debug
```

## UI Development

### 1. Setup Your Local UI Development Environment

```bash
# Clone the repo (if you haven't already)
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/litellm.git
cd litellm

# Navigate to the UI dashboard directory
cd ui/litellm-dashboard

# Install dependencies
npm install

# Start the development server
npm run dev
```

### 2. Adding UI Tests

If you are adding a **new component** or **new logic**, you must add corresponding tests.

### 3. Running UI Unit Tests

```bash
npm run test
```

### 4. Building the UI

Ensure the UI builds successfully before submitting your PR:

```bash
npm run build
```

## Submitting Your PR

1. **Push your branch**: `git push origin your-feature-branch`
2. **Create a PR**: Go to GitHub and open a pull request against [`litellm_internal_staging`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/litellm_internal_staging), which is the default base branch. Do not target `main`.
3. **Fill out the PR template**: Provide clear description of changes
4. **Wait for review**: Maintainers will review and provide feedback
5. **Address feedback**: Make requested changes and push updates
6. **Merge**: Once approved, your PR will be merged!

## Getting Help

If you need help:

- 💬 [Join our Discord](https://discord.gg/wuPM9dRgDw)
- 💬 [Join our Slack](https://www.litellm.ai/support)
- 📧 Email us: ishaan@berri.ai / krrish@berri.ai
- 🐛 [Create an issue](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/new)

## What to Contribute

Looking for ideas? Check out:

- 🐛 [Good first issues](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/labels/good%20first%20issue)
- 🚀 [Feature requests](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/labels/enhancement)
- 📚 Documentation improvements
- 🧪 Test coverage improvements
- 🔌 New LLM provider integrations

Thank you for contributing to LiteLLM! 🚀
