    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Known Issues & Workarounds Index (Support + CS Landing)\",\n  \"space\": \"customer-success-and-support\",\n  \"author\": \"Elliot Price\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"customer-success\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-10\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-15\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Dev Patel\",\n    \"Rachel Kim\",\n    \"Sean Gallagher\",\n    \"Priya Natarajan\",\n    \"Wei Chen\",\n    \"Kira Thompson\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"support\",\n    \"customer-success\",\n    \"known-issues\",\n    \"workarounds\",\n    \"troubleshooting\",\n    \"escalations\",\n    \"sla\",\n    \"incident-comms\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/severity-matrix-and-escalation-triggers\",\n    \"/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/sla-policy-by-customer-tier\",\n    \"/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/escalation-paths-and-contacts-2026\",\n    \"/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/slack-bridge-and-incident-channel-conventions\",\n    \"/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-triage-intake-checklist\",\n    \"/customer-success-and-support/support-process/jira-field-guidelines-and-sla-timers\",\n    \"/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/customer-incident-comms-alignment\",\n    \"/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/support-sla-vs-engineering-slo-mapping\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"content\": \"## Purpose\\nThis page is the landing index for **Known Issues & Workarounds** used by **Support** and **Customer Success**. It is optimized for:\\n- Faster triage (copy/paste symptoms + quick checks)\\n- Lower repeat ticket volume (consistent workaround guidance)\\n- Clear escalation decisions (when to page SRE/Eng vs continue troubleshooting)\\n\\nThis index only includes issues that meet the **Known Issue publication criteria**: reproducible symptoms, validated workaround (or clear mitigation limits), and named owner + review cadence.\\n\\n> Customer-sensitive details (account identifiers, internal hostnames, customer-specific configs) must not be added to KB pages or this index.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## How to use this index (Support/CS)\\n1) Identify the best matching issue by **symptom** and **tags** (tier/region/model).\\n2) Follow the linked **workaround article** and use the relevant **Support macro/snippet**.\\n3) If escalation criteria are met, escalate using:\\n   - **Severity Matrix + Escalation Triggers** (P0\\u2013P4 \\u2194 Sev mapping)\\n   - **SLA policy by customer tier** (response + update cadence)\\n   - **Slack bridge conventions** (when to move to #incidents)\\n4) Add the KB link to the ticket and include what was tried.\\n\\n**Support workflow expectation:** When a ticket matches an entry below, link the KB article in the Jira ticket (SUP) and record:\\n- Which workaround steps were attempted\\n- Result (resolved / partial / no change)\\n- Whether escalation criteria were met\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Tags and terminology\\n**Tier tags**\\n- Hosted = Redwood API (self-serve + enterprise Hosted)\\n- Dedicated = Dedicated GPU pools\\n- Private = VPC / on-prem\\n\\n**Region tags (examples)**\\n- us-east, us-west, eu-west\\n\\n**Model tags (examples)**\\n- Any = model-agnostic (gateway/SDK/network/control plane)\\n- Embeddings = embeddings endpoints\\n- Chat/Completion = streaming/non-streaming generation\\n\\n**Status tags**\\n- Active = currently observed recently and still possible\\n- Mitigated = mitigation in place; may recur under certain conditions\\n- Fixed pending rollout = fix merged/released but not fully rolled out\\n- Resolved = no longer expected; keep for 30\\u201360 days as reference\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Escalation guidance (applies to all known issues)\\nEscalate using the standard escalation playbook; do not bypass incident processes.\\n\\n**Escalate immediately (page on-call / start bridge) if any are true:**\\n- Customer impact meets **P0/P1** criteria (see Severity Matrix)\\n- Error rate spike / hard outage is suspected (auth failures, widespread 5xx, widespread timeouts)\\n- Multi-customer/regional impact or credible revenue/SLA risk\\n- Customer reports security/compliance risk (audit logs, access control) and is enterprise/private\\n\\n**Escalate after initial checks if:**\\n- Workaround steps were applied correctly and **no improvement**\\n- We cannot confirm telemetry signals (missing request IDs/region/model, or inconsistent metrics)\\n- Symptoms deviate materially from the known issue description\\n\\n**Before escalating, include (minimum context):**\\n- Request IDs (or sample request IDs), timestamps (with timezone), region, model, endpoint\\n- SDK + version, streaming vs non-streaming, retries/timeouts config\\n- Customer tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and support coverage window\\n- Any recent change noted by customer (SDK upgrade, deploy, routing policy changes)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Index of Known Issues (curated)\\n> Tip: When opening a Slack bridge, paste the relevant workaround link and the \\u201cEscalate when\\u201d line.\\n\\n| Known issue | Symptoms (customer-visible) | Affected tags | Workaround / KB | Status | Last updated | Primary owner | When to escalate |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|\\n| Streaming timeouts / disconnects (reset or truncated stream) | Stream resets mid-generation, truncated output, client sees ECONNRESET / incomplete chunks | Tier: Hosted, Dedicated \\u00b7 Region: us-east (most reports), Any \\u00b7 Model: Chat/Completion (streaming) | /customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/workaround-streaming-timeouts-and-reconnect | Active | 2026-02-14 | Owen Phillips (Support Incidents) | Escalate if reproducible on Redwood sample clients, >1 customer affected in 60 min, or any enterprise account blocked; escalate immediately if error rate spike/regional pattern suspected. |\\n| 429 quota mismatch / confusing rate-limit headers | Customer sees 429s after SDK upgrade; headers inconsistent vs Console quota; perceived \\u201cunexpected throttling\\u201d | Tier: Hosted \\u00b7 Region: Any \\u00b7 Model: Any | /customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/workaround-429-quota-mismatch-and-rate-limit-headers | Fixed pending rollout | 2026-02-13 | Ethan Park (Platform) | Escalate if headers are inconsistent across endpoints in same time window, or if customer is hard-blocked despite low observed usage; attach header samples + request IDs. |\\n| Dedicated autoscaling oscillation causing latency spikes | Latency spikes + throughput drops correlated with scale up/down churn; uneven tail lat | Tier: Dedicated \\u00b7 Region: Any \\u00b7 Model: Any | /customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/workaround-dedicated-autoscaling-oscillation | Mitigated | 2026-02-14 | Sean Gallagher (SRE) | Escalate if p95 latency breaches customer SLO for >15 min, replicas flap repeatedly despite cooldown changes, or if capacity/burst not activating as configured. |\\n| Private installer upgrade stuck at migrations | Upgrade hangs or fails during migration step; rollback uncertainty; repeated retries worsen | Tier: Private \\u00b7 Region: Customer VPC/on-prem \\u00b7 Model: N/A | /customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/workaround-private-installer-upgrade-stuck-migrations | Active | 2026-02-12 | Priya Natarajan (Platform) | Escalate immediately if production Private deployment is blocked, rollback is required, or customer is in a regulated window; collect diagnostics bundle/logs per article before paging. |\\n| Audit log delivery latency (lag > expected) | Audit logs delayed (e.g., 15\\u201360+ min), customer compliance concerns, SIEM pipeline appears stale | Tier: Hosted Enterprise, Private \\u00b7 Region: Any \\u00b7 Model: N/A | /customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/workaround-audit-log-delivery-latency | Active | 2026-02-14 | Allison Grant (Observability) | Escalate if lag exceeds enterprise expectation threshold (per SLA policy), if multiple accounts show lag, or if customer states compliance breach risk; include timestamps + tenant/org ID via secure internal channel only. |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Additional high-frequency issues (candidate / watchlist)\\nThese are **not** fully published as Known Issues unless linked to a KB article with validated workaround. Keep an eye on trend changes and file tickets with consistent repro info.\\n\\n| Issue (watchlist) | Symptoms | Tags | Current guidance | Owner | Last reviewed |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---:|\\n| Model version pin perceived \\u201cignored\\u201d during fallback | Customer expects pinned version but sees different behavior during degradation | Tier: Hosted/Dedicated \\u00b7 Region: Any \\u00b7 Model: Any | Use routing metrics + policy review; confirm fallback configuration and whether pinned version allows compatible variants. Escalate if metrics show fallback contradicts policy. | Mina Haddad | 2026-02-15 |\\n| Console latency dashboard missing region breakdown | eu-west (or other region) missing from Console filters; customers ask for interim reporting | Tier: Hosted/Dedicated \\u00b7 Region: Console \\u00b7 Model: N/A | Provide interim metrics export guidance; open Platform telemetry ticket if confirmed. | Ethan Park | 2026-02-15 |\\n| Embeddings endpoint timeouts (eu-west) | Increased timeout rate; customer sees retries and degraded throughput | Tier: Hosted \\u00b7 Region: eu-west \\u00b7 Model: Embeddings | Follow triage checklist; if multiple customers affected, move to #incidents and consider status-page criteria. | Sean Gallagher | 2026-02-15 |\\n| SAML SSO login loop in Console | Redirect loop after IdP login, cannot access Console | Tier: Enterprise Hosted/Private \\u00b7 Region: Any \\u00b7 Model: N/A | Collect IdP metadata + Console auth logs request; escalate to Control Plane if reproducible. | Ethan Park | 2026-02-15 |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Maintenance policy (ownership + freshness)\\n- Each Known Issue must have a **Primary owner** and at least one **reviewer**.\\n- Owners review entries **weekly during the sprint window** and **biweekly** afterwards.\\n- If an issue is marked **Fixed pending rollout**, update this index once rollout is complete and record the date.\\n- If an issue becomes **Resolved**, keep it listed for **30\\u201360 days** with a note pointing to the fix/release, then remove from the index.\\n\\n**Change control:**\\n- Edits that change escalation thresholds or SLA language require review from **Support Ops (Dev Patel)** and **SRE (Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes)**.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Where to link this from\\n- Jira SUP ticket templates/macros (auto-suggest this index for new tickets)\\n- Support triage intake checklist\\n- Slack bridge workflow pinned message\\n- CS QBR prep checklist (link relevant known issues for top accounts)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Changelog (recent)\\n- 2026-02-15: Added watchlist section; clarified escalation minimum context; refreshed owners/reviewers. (Elliot Price)\\n- 2026-02-14: Published initial set of sprint-known issues (streaming, 429/quota, Dedicated autoscaling, Private upgrade, audit log lag). document.title: Known Issues & Workarounds Index (Support + CS Landing)
document.content:
{
  "title": "Known Issues & Workarounds Index (Support + CS Landing)",
  "space": "customer-success-and-support",
  "author": "Elliot Price",
  "owner_team": "customer-success",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-02-10",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-15",
  "reviewers": [
    "Dev Patel",
    "Rachel Kim",
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Priya Natarajan",
    "Wei Chen",
    "Kira Thompson"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "support",
    "customer-success",
    "known-issues",
    "workarounds",
    "troubleshooting",
    "escalations",
    "sla",
    "incident-comms"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/severity-matrix-and-escalation-triggers",
    "/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/sla-policy-by-customer-tier",
    "/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/escalation-paths-and-contacts-2026",
    "/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/slack-bridge-and-incident-channel-conventions",
    "/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-triage-intake-checklist",
    "/customer-success-and-support/support-process/jira-field-guidelines-and-sla-timers",
    "/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/customer-incident-comms-alignment",
    "/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/support-sla-vs-engineering-slo-mapping"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "content": "## Purpose
This page is the landing index for **Known Issues & Workarounds** used by **Support** and **Customer Success**. It is optimized for:
- Faster triage (copy/paste symptoms + quick checks)
- Lower repeat ticket volume (consistent workaround guidance)
- Clear escalation decisions (when to page SRE/Eng vs continue troubleshooting)

This index only includes issues that meet the **Known Issue publication criteria**: reproducible symptoms, validated workaround (or clear mitigation limits), and named owner + review cadence.

> Customer-sensitive details (account identifiers, internal hostnames, customer-specific configs) must not be added to KB pages or this index.

---

## How to use this index (Support/CS)
1) Identify the best matching issue by **symptom** and **tags** (tier/region/model).
2) Follow the linked **workaround article** and use the relevant **Support macro/snippet**.
3) If escalation criteria are met, escalate using:
   - **Severity Matrix + Escalation Triggers** (P0–P4 ↔ Sev mapping)
   - **SLA policy by customer tier** (response + update cadence)
   - **Slack bridge conventions** (when to move to #incidents)
4) Add the KB link to the ticket and include what was tried.

**Support workflow expectation:** When a ticket matches an entry below, link the KB article in the Jira ticket (SUP) and record:
- Which workaround steps were attempted
- Result (resolved / partial / no change)
- Whether escalation criteria were met

---

## Tags and terminology
**Tier tags**
- Hosted = Redwood API (self-serve + enterprise Hosted)
- Dedicated = Dedicated GPU pools
- Private = VPC / on-prem

**Region tags (examples)**
- us-east, us-west, eu-west

**Model tags (examples)**
- Any = model-agnostic (gateway/SDK/network/control plane)
- Embeddings = embeddings endpoints
- Chat/Completion = streaming/non-streaming generation

**Status tags**
- Active = currently observed recently and still possible
- Mitigated = mitigation in place; may recur under certain conditions
- Fixed pending rollout = fix merged/released but not fully rolled out
- Resolved = no longer expected; keep for 30–60 days as reference

---

## Escalation guidance (applies to all known issues)
Escalate using the standard escalation playbook; do not bypass incident processes.

**Escalate immediately (page on-call / start bridge) if any are true:**
- Customer impact meets **P0/P1** criteria (see Severity Matrix)
- Error rate spike / hard outage is suspected (auth failures, widespread 5xx, widespread timeouts)
- Multi-customer/regional impact or credible revenue/SLA risk
- Customer reports security/compliance risk (audit logs, access control) and is enterprise/private

**Escalate after initial checks if:**
- Workaround steps were applied correctly and **no improvement**
- We cannot confirm telemetry signals (missing request IDs/region/model, or inconsistent metrics)
- Symptoms deviate materially from the known issue description

**Before escalating, include (minimum context):**
- Request IDs (or sample request IDs), timestamps (with timezone), region, model, endpoint
- SDK + version, streaming vs non-streaming, retries/timeouts config
- Customer tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and support coverage window
- Any recent change noted by customer (SDK upgrade, deploy, routing policy changes)

---

## Index of Known Issues (curated)
> Tip: When opening a Slack bridge, paste the relevant workaround link and the “Escalate when” line.

| Known issue | Symptoms (customer-visible) | Affected tags | Workaround / KB | Status | Last updated | Primary owner | When to escalate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Streaming timeouts / disconnects (reset or truncated stream) | Stream resets mid-generation, truncated output, client sees ECONNRESET / incomplete chunks | Tier: Hosted, Dedicated · Region: us-east (most reports), Any · Model: Chat/Completion (streaming) | /customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/workaround-streaming-timeouts-and-reconnect | Active | 2026-02-14 | Owen Phillips (Support Incidents) | Escalate if reproducible on Redwood sample clients, >1 customer affected in 60 min, or any enterprise account blocked; escalate immediately if error rate spike/regional pattern suspected. |
| 429 quota mismatch / confusing rate-limit headers | Customer sees 429s after SDK upgrade; headers inconsistent vs Console quota; perceived “unexpected throttling” | Tier: Hosted · Region: Any · Model: Any | /customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/workaround-429-quota-mismatch-and-rate-limit-headers | Fixed pending rollout | 2026-02-13 | Ethan Park (Platform) | Escalate if headers are inconsistent across endpoints in same time window, or if customer is hard-blocked despite low observed usage; attach header samples + request IDs. |
| Dedicated autoscaling oscillation causing latency spikes | Latency spikes + throughput drops correlated with scale up/down churn; uneven tail lat | Tier: Dedicated · Region: Any · Model: Any | /customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/workaround-dedicated-autoscaling-oscillation | Mitigated | 2026-02-14 | Sean Gallagher (SRE) | Escalate if p95 latency breaches customer SLO for >15 min, replicas flap repeatedly despite cooldown changes, or if capacity/burst not activating as configured. |
| Private installer upgrade stuck at migrations | Upgrade hangs or fails during migration step; rollback uncertainty; repeated retries worsen | Tier: Private · Region: Customer VPC/on-prem · Model: N/A | /customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/workaround-private-installer-upgrade-stuck-migrations | Active | 2026-02-12 | Priya Natarajan (Platform) | Escalate immediately if production Private deployment is blocked, rollback is required, or customer is in a regulated window; collect diagnostics bundle/logs per article before paging. |
| Audit log delivery latency (lag > expected) | Audit logs delayed (e.g., 15–60+ min), customer compliance concerns, SIEM pipeline appears stale | Tier: Hosted Enterprise, Private · Region: Any · Model: N/A | /customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/workaround-audit-log-delivery-latency | Active | 2026-02-14 | Allison Grant (Observability) | Escalate if lag exceeds enterprise expectation threshold (per SLA policy), if multiple accounts show lag, or if customer states compliance breach risk; include timestamps + tenant/org ID via secure internal channel only. |

---

## Additional high-frequency issues (candidate / watchlist)
These are **not** fully published as Known Issues unless linked to a KB article with validated workaround. Keep an eye on trend changes and file tickets with consistent repro info.

| Issue (watchlist) | Symptoms | Tags | Current guidance | Owner | Last reviewed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Model version pin perceived “ignored” during fallback | Customer expects pinned version but sees different behavior during degradation | Tier: Hosted/Dedicated · Region: Any · Model: Any | Use routing metrics + policy review; confirm fallback configuration and whether pinned version allows compatible variants. Escalate if metrics show fallback contradicts policy. | Mina Haddad | 2026-02-15 |
| Console latency dashboard missing region breakdown | eu-west (or other region) missing from Console filters; customers ask for interim reporting | Tier: Hosted/Dedicated · Region: Console · Model: N/A | Provide interim metrics export guidance; open Platform telemetry ticket if confirmed. | Ethan Park | 2026-02-15 |
| Embeddings endpoint timeouts (eu-west) | Increased timeout rate; customer sees retries and degraded throughput | Tier: Hosted · Region: eu-west · Model: Embeddings | Follow triage checklist; if multiple customers affected, move to #incidents and consider status-page criteria. | Sean Gallagher | 2026-02-15 |
| SAML SSO login loop in Console | Redirect loop after IdP login, cannot access Console | Tier: Enterprise Hosted/Private · Region: Any · Model: N/A | Collect IdP metadata + Console auth logs request; escalate to Control Plane if reproducible. | Ethan Park | 2026-02-15 |

---

## Maintenance policy (ownership + freshness)
- Each Known Issue must have a **Primary owner** and at least one **reviewer**.
- Owners review entries **weekly during the sprint window** and **biweekly** afterwards.
- If an issue is marked **Fixed pending rollout**, update this index once rollout is complete and record the date.
- If an issue becomes **Resolved**, keep it listed for **30–60 days** with a note pointing to the fix/release, then remove from the index.

**Change control:**
- Edits that change escalation thresholds or SLA language require review from **Support Ops (Dev Patel)** and **SRE (Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes)**.

---

## Where to link this from
- Jira SUP ticket templates/macros (auto-suggest this index for new tickets)
- Support triage intake checklist
- Slack bridge workflow pinned message
- CS QBR prep checklist (link relevant known issues for top accounts)

---

## Changelog (recent)
- 2026-02-15: Added watchlist section; clarified escalation minimum context; refreshed owners/reviewers. (Elliot Price)
- 2026-02-14: Published initial set of sprint-known issues (streaming, 429/quota, Dedicated autoscaling, Private upgrade, audit log lag). (Docs/Support/Eng reviewers)

    "id": "dsid_6b8cf1a56ff7450cae5a435ab6499c28",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/linear/design/DES-755-rollout-timeline-and-audit-activity-panel.json",
    "title": "Hosted canary rollout: customer-visible timeline + audit activity panel",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"DES-755\",\n  \"team\": \"design\",\n  \"title\": \"Hosted canary rollout: customer-visible timeline + audit activity panel\",\n  \"status\": \"In Review\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-21\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-03-25\",\n  \"creator\": \"Tessa Morgan\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Kenji Nakamura\",\n  \"project\": \"Hosted canary rollout workflow (GA)\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W09\",\n  \"estimate\": \"5\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-03-28\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"Console\",\n    \"Rollouts\",\n    \"Hosted\",\n    \"GA\",\n    \"Timeline\",\n    \"Auditability\",\n    \"Approvals\",\n    \"Auto-rollback\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"DES-742\",\n    \"DES-763\",\n    \"PM-1843\",\n    \"PM-1851\",\n    \"ENG-9140\",\n    \"ENG-9171\"\n  ],\n  \"sub_issues\": [\n    \"DES-755-a\",\n    \"DES-755-b\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"console-2025.04\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"true\",\n  \"description\": \"Goal\\nDesign the rollout details experience for Hosted canary rollouts, focusing on two tightly-related surfaces:\\n1) Rollout timeline: a clear step-by-step visualization of traffic split progression (1% \\u2192 5% \\u2192 25% \\u2192 50% \\u2192 100%), including state transitions (scheduled, running, soaking, paused, approval required, auto-stopped, rolled back, completed).\\n2) Activity panel: an audit-like, customer-visible history of actions and system events (who did what, when, and why), with enough detail to support change control and debugging without exposing internal-only data.\\n\\nWhy this matters\\n- During beta, customers repeatedly asked \\u201cwhat happened and why did it pause/rollback?\\u201d and support escalations had to correlate control plane events + SRE notes.\\n- GA scope includes customer-visible timeline + change history, plus alignment with audit log events (Security) for regulated customers.\\n\\nPrimary users\\n- ML/platform engineers running rollouts on production routes\\n- Admins/approvers (enterprise governance)\\n- On-call/SRE + support investigating issues with a customer\\n\\nEntry points\\n- Console > Hosted Routes > Route Details > Rollouts tab > Rollout details page\\n- Console notification / banner linking to a rollout that paused / needs approval\\n\\nInformation architecture (proposed)\\n- Header: Rollout name, route, baseline model+version, canary model+version, current status badge, started by, start time, region scope summary.\\n- Primary tabs/sections:\\n  A) Timeline (default)\\n  B) Metrics (baseline vs canary) (DES-763)\\n  C) Activity (audit-like) (this ticket; may also appear as a right panel on Timeline)\\n\\nTimeline design (step-centric)\\n- Timeline is a vertical, chronological list of \\u201cStep cards\\u201d with a compact progress indicator.\\n- Each step card includes:\\n  - Target split (e.g., Canary 5% / Baseline 95%) and step number\\n  - State (Scheduled / Running / Soaking / Completed / Paused / Failed / Rolled back)\\n  - Soak requirement and actual soak duration elapsed (e.g., \\u201cMin soak: 30m\\u201d + a timer)\\n  - Guardrails summary (max step, approvals enabled, auto-stop thresholds enabled)\\n  - Primary actions (contextual): Pause, Resume, Advance, Rollback (subject to permissions)\\n  - \\u201cView metrics for this step\\u201d deep link that pre-filters cohort comparison to the step window\\n\\nState model (customer-visible wording)\\n- Draft: created but not started\\n- Running: traffic split is actively applied\\n- Soaking: split is stable and waiting on min soak time (or approval gate)\\n- Approval required: needs an approver to proceed to next step (explicit gate)\\n- Paused: user-initiated pause\\n- Auto-paused: system paused due to stop condition evaluation (pre-rollback) or metric evaluation failure (see edge cases)\\n- Rolled back: traffic returned to baseline (100% baseline)\\n- Completed: reached final target (typically 100% canary) and rollout marked complete\\n\\nCopy guidance (align with DES-742 warnings)\\n- \\u201cAuto-paused\\u201d vs \\u201cAuto-stopped\\u201d: propose \\u201cAuto-paused\\u201d for temporary halts where customer can resume after review; reserve \\u201cAuto-rolled back\\u201d for destructive/automatic return-to-baseline.\\n- When displaying auto events, always include a reason line and a \\u2018Review stop condition\\u2019 link to thresholds.\\n\\nApproval gates\\n- Timeline should show an \\u201cApproval checkpoint\\u201d row between steps when enabled.\\n- Approval checkpoint row includes:\\n  - Required role (e.g., Rollout approver)\\n  - \\u201cRequested by\\u201d + timestamp\\n  - Approver action (Approve step / Reject + rollback suggestion)\\n  - Optional comment field (stored in activity history)\\n\\nAuto-stop / auto-rollback\\n- Timeline should surface the stop condition that triggered the system action:\\n  - Signal (5xx rate, timeouts, p95 latency regression)\\n  - Threshold and observed value (customer-facing; avoid internal metric names)\\n  - Evaluation window (e.g., \\u201cover last 10 minutes\\u201d)\\n  - Resulting action (Auto-paused / Auto-rolled back)\\n- Include a prominent \\u201cRollback completed\\u201d banner when rollback occurs, with a \\u2018What changed\\u2019 link that summarizes traffic returning to baseline.\\n\\nActivity panel (audit-like history)\\n- Activity is an append-only event feed with:\\n  - Timestamp (absolute + relative)\\n  - Actor (user name + org role, or \\u201cSystem\\u201d)\\n  - Action label (Created rollout, Started rollout, Advanced to step, Paused, Resumed, Approval requested, Approved, Auto-paused, Auto-rolled back, Rollback initiated, Rollback completed, Threshold updated)\\n  - Details snippet (diff-like: \\u201cSplit: 95/5 \\u2192 75/25\\u201d, \\u201cMin soak: 30m \\u2192 60m\\u201d)\\n  - Optional reason/comment (user-entered; required for destructive actions per UX)\\n  - Links: \\u201cView metrics at this time\\u201d, \\u201cView config\\u201d (read-only JSON view), \\u201cView audit log event\\u201d (if tenant has Audit Logs feature)\\n\\nActivity types to include (v1)\\n- Rollout lifecycle: create, start, complete, cancel\\n- Step changes: advance, revert to previous step (if supported), pause/resume\\n- Governance: approval requested, approved, rejected\\n- System: stop condition triggered, metric evaluation timed out, enforcement discrepancy detected (customer-friendly wording)\\n- Policy: action blocked by policy (should appear as UI toast, but also as an activity entry only if an action was attempted and denied)\\n\\nActivity vs Audit Logs (important distinction)\\n- Activity panel is customer-visible and intended for debugging + operational transparency.\\n- Audit logs are security/compliance-grade and exported; activity panel should link to audit event IDs when available, but not imply it is the system-of-record.\\n- Proposed UI copy under Activity header: \\u201cActivity shows a history of rollout actions and system events. For compliance audit logs, see Audit Logs.\\u201d (Only show second sentence if feature enabled.)\\n\\nEmpty/error states\\n- If metrics are delayed: timeline still renders step transitions, but shows \\u201cMetrics pending\\u201d badges with last update time.\\n- If an event lacks an actor (legacy/backfill): show \\u201cUnknown actor\\u201d with tooltip.\\n- If user lacks permission: show timeline read-only; actions hidden; activity still visible.\\n\\nEdge cases (from beta + SRE feedback)\\n- Metric evaluation timeout caused step to appear \\u2018stuck\\u2019: timeline should show a \\u2018Needs attention\\u2019 callout with suggested actions (retry evaluation / pause / rollback) and a \\u201cLast evaluation attempt\\u201d timestamp.\\n- Split mismatch by region (enforcement lag): show a warning banner \\u201cTraffic split not fully applied in all regions yet\\u201d with region-level status (collapsed by default). Avoid listing per-AZ.\\n- Streaming retries: do not show \\u201cdouble-counted\\u201d step transitions; activity is based on orchestrator events only.\\n\\nAccessibility + internationalization\\n- Timeline must be navigable via keyboard; state indicated via both color and text.\\n- Use consistent badge shapes for status.\\n- Timestamps in user locale; show UTC on hover.\\n\\nDeliverables\\n- Figma: rollout timeline step cards, approval checkpoint row, banners for auto events, and activity feed patterns\\n- Interaction spec: state transitions and action availability matrix by status + permission\\n- Copy deck for auto-pause/rollback reasons + destructive confirmations\\n\\nLinks\\n- Wizard flow: DES-742\\n- Metrics view: DES-763\\n- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd.json\\n- Design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/hosted-canary-rollout-workflow-design-spec.json\\n- Audit events spec: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-events-rollout-actions.json\\n\\nOpen questions\\n1) Do we show \\u2018auto-paused\\u2019 and \\u2018auto-rolled back\\u2019 as separate terminal statuses, or show status + last event? Current recommendation: status is the state; events explain the reason.\\n2) Should activity include policy/permission denials? Proposed: only when a user attempted an action (so it\\u2019s traceable), not for background policy evaluations.\\n3) Should approvals appear in both Timeline and Activity? Proposed: yes (Timeline shows current checkpoint; Activity is the record).\\n4) Do we allow adding a comment after an auto-pause to document decision-making? Proposed: add \\u201cAdd note\\u201d action (non-audit) if easy; otherwise GA follow-up.\\n\\nAcceptance criteria\\n- A customer can answer: What step are we on? What percent is canary? How long have we been soaking? Why are we paused? Who approved? When did rollback happen?\\n- Timeline reflects all major lifecycle transitions in a human-readable way.\\n- Activity entries map cleanly to audit events (ENG-9171) and include a stable event ID when available.\\n- Works in read-only mode for users without rollout permissions.\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-02-21 (Tessa Morgan): Spinning this off from DES-742. Beta feedback: customers loved the wizard but had no confidence post-start; they want a \\u2018flight recorder\\u2019 view. Need tight alignment with audit events + orchestrator state machine.\",\n    \"2025-02-24 (Kenji Nakamura): Draft IA: Rollout details page with Timeline + Metrics + Activity. Question: do we make Activity a right-side panel on Timeline to reduce navigation? Testing both options in Figma.\",\n    \"2025-02-26 (Marissa Cole): +1 on activity being visible without audit-log entitlement, but language must avoid promising compliance-grade logs. Also want an approval checkpoint row that\\u2019s obvious (some customers missed approval gates in other workflows).\",\n    \"2025-02-28 (Marcus Lin): Please ensure we can display \\u2018Audit Event ID\\u2019 (or link) when Audit Logs are enabled. Also: actor should include auth principal type (user vs service account) if we support service accounts initiating rollouts.\",\n    \"2025-03-03 (Sean Gallagher): For auto-pause/rollback, we need reason text that\\u2019s actionable and non-alarming. Ex: \\u201cp95 latency exceeded threshold\\u201d + show window + observed values. Avoid internal metric names like \\u2018rw.http.server.latency.p95\\u2019.\",\n    \"2025-03-06 (Nora Ahmed): Implementation note: timeline needs a \\u2018system\\u2019 row type that isn\\u2019t a step. Orchestrator emits events that don\\u2019t correspond 1:1 to steps (e.g., evaluation retries). Design should support that without confusing customers.\",\n    \"2025-03-11 (Kenji Nakamura): Added \\u2018Needs attention\\u2019 banner for metric-eval timeout / stuck conditions. Banner includes: last evaluation attempt, suggested next actions, and link to runbook (internal only). Need to confirm what\\u2019s customer-facing.\",\n    \"2025-03-14 (Felix Schneider): For Activity diffs, avoid showing raw JSON in the feed; show compact diffs with a \\u2018View config\\u2019 drawer for full detail. This helps keep the feed readable and reduces risk of leaking internal fields.\",\n    \"2025-03-18 (Tessa Morgan): Copy review based on design Slack thread: prefer \\u2018Auto-paused\\u2019 (temporary) vs \\u2018Auto-rolled back\\u2019 (destructive). Add confirmation modal copy for manual rollback requiring a reason/comment (stored in Activity).\",\n    \"2025-03-21 (Kenji Nakamura): Marking In Review. Figma links shared in #design for review. Pending: finalize region-scope warning pattern (split mismatch) and the wording for \\u2018Unknown actor\\u2019/legacy events.\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_6b8cf1a56ff7450cae5a435ab6499c28\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted canary rollout: customer-visible timeline + audit activity panel\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/design/DES-755-rollout-timeline-and-audit-activity-panel.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: design\nProject: Hosted canary rollout workflow (GA)\nTeam: design\n\ntimeline design ( step - centric ) - timeline is a vertical, chronological list of “ step cards ” with a compact progress indicator. - each step card includes : - target split ( e. g., canary 5 % / baseline 95 % ) and step number - state ( scheduled / running / soaking / completed / paused / failed / rolled back ) - soak requirement and actual soak duration elapsed ( e. g., “ min soak : 30m ” + a timer ) - guardrails summary ( max step, approvals enabled, auto - stop thresholds enabled ) - primary actions ( contextual ) : pause, resume, advance, rollback ( subject to permissions ) - “ view metrics for this step ” deep link that pre - filters cohort comparison",

document.title: Hosted canary rollout: customer-visible timeline + audit activity panel
document.content:
{
  "key": "DES-755",
  "team": "design",
  "title": "Hosted canary rollout: customer-visible timeline + audit activity panel",
  "status": "In Review",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2025-02-21",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-25",
  "creator": "Tessa Morgan",
  "assignee": "Kenji Nakamura",
  "project": "Hosted canary rollout workflow (GA)",
  "cycle": "2025-W09",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2025-03-28",
  "labels": [
    "Console",
    "Rollouts",
    "Hosted",
    "GA",
    "Timeline",
    "Auditability",
    "Approvals",
    "Auto-rollback"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "DES-742",
    "DES-763",
    "PM-1843",
    "PM-1851",
    "ENG-9140",
    "ENG-9171"
  ],
  "sub_issues": [
    "DES-755-a",
    "DES-755-b"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "console-2025.04",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "description": "Goal
Design the rollout details experience for Hosted canary rollouts, focusing on two tightly-related surfaces:
1) Rollout timeline: a clear step-by-step visualization of traffic split progression (1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%), including state transitions (scheduled, running, soaking, paused, approval required, auto-stopped, rolled back, completed).
2) Activity panel: an audit-like, customer-visible history of actions and system events (who did what, when, and why), with enough detail to support change control and debugging without exposing internal-only data.

Why this matters
- During beta, customers repeatedly asked “what happened and why did it pause/rollback?” and support escalations had to correlate control plane events + SRE notes.
- GA scope includes customer-visible timeline + change history, plus alignment with audit log events (Security) for regulated customers.

Primary users
- ML/platform engineers running rollouts on production routes
- Admins/approvers (enterprise governance)
- On-call/SRE + support investigating issues with a customer

Entry points
- Console > Hosted Routes > Route Details > Rollouts tab > Rollout details page
- Console notification / banner linking to a rollout that paused / needs approval

Information architecture (proposed)
- Header: Rollout name, route, baseline model+version, canary model+version, current status badge, started by, start time, region scope summary.
- Primary tabs/sections:
  A) Timeline (default)
  B) Metrics (baseline vs canary) (DES-763)
  C) Activity (audit-like) (this ticket; may also appear as a right panel on Timeline)

Timeline design (step-centric)
- Timeline is a vertical, chronological list of “Step cards” with a compact progress indicator.
- Each step card includes:
  - Target split (e.g., Canary 5% / Baseline 95%) and step number
  - State (Scheduled / Running / Soaking / Completed / Paused / Failed / Rolled back)
  - Soak requirement and actual soak duration elapsed (e.g., “Min soak: 30m” + a timer)
  - Guardrails summary (max step, approvals enabled, auto-stop thresholds enabled)
  - Primary actions (contextual): Pause, Resume, Advance, Rollback (subject to permissions)
  - “View metrics for this step” deep link that pre-filters cohort comparison to the step window

State model (customer-visible wording)
- Draft: created but not started
- Running: traffic split is actively applied
- Soaking: split is stable and waiting on min soak time (or approval gate)
- Approval required: needs an approver to proceed to next step (explicit gate)
- Paused: user-initiated pause
- Auto-paused: system paused due to stop condition evaluation (pre-rollback) or metric evaluation failure (see edge cases)
- Rolled back: traffic returned to baseline (100% baseline)
- Completed: reached final target (typically 100% canary) and rollout marked complete

Copy guidance (align with DES-742 warnings)
- “Auto-paused” vs “Auto-stopped”: propose “Auto-paused” for temporary halts where customer can resume after review; reserve “Auto-rolled back” for destructive/automatic return-to-baseline.
- When displaying auto events, always include a reason line and a ‘Review stop condition’ link to thresholds.

Approval gates
- Timeline should show an “Approval checkpoint” row between steps when enabled.
- Approval checkpoint row includes:
  - Required role (e.g., Rollout approver)
  - “Requested by” + timestamp
  - Approver action (Approve step / Reject + rollback suggestion)
  - Optional comment field (stored in activity history)

Auto-stop / auto-rollback
- Timeline should surface the stop condition that triggered the system action:
  - Signal (5xx rate, timeouts, p95 latency regression)
  - Threshold and observed value (customer-facing; avoid internal metric names)
  - Evaluation window (e.g., “over last 10 minutes”)
  - Resulting action (Auto-paused / Auto-rolled back)
- Include a prominent “Rollback completed” banner when rollback occurs, with a ‘What changed’ link that summarizes traffic returning to baseline.

Activity panel (audit-like history)
- Activity is an append-only event feed with:
  - Timestamp (absolute + relative)
  - Actor (user name + org role, or “System”)
  - Action label (Created rollout, Started rollout, Advanced to step, Paused, Resumed, Approval requested, Approved, Auto-paused, Auto-rolled back, Rollback initiated, Rollback completed, Threshold updated)
  - Details snippet (diff-like: “Split: 95/5 → 75/25”, “Min soak: 30m → 60m”)
  - Optional reason/comment (user-entered; required for destructive actions per UX)
  - Links: “View metrics at this time”, “View config” (read-only JSON view), “View audit log event” (if tenant has Audit Logs feature)

Activity types to include (v1)
- Rollout lifecycle: create, start, complete, cancel
- Step changes: advance, revert to previous step (if supported), pause/resume
- Governance: approval requested, approved, rejected
- System: stop condition triggered, metric evaluation timed out, enforcement discrepancy detected (customer-friendly wording)
- Policy: action blocked by policy (should appear as UI toast, but also as an activity entry only if an action was attempted and denied)

Activity vs Audit Logs (important distinction)
- Activity panel is customer-visible and intended for debugging + operational transparency.
- Audit logs are security/compliance-grade and exported; activity panel should link to audit event IDs when available, but not imply it is the system-of-record.
- Proposed UI copy under Activity header: “Activity shows a history of rollout actions and system events. For compliance audit logs, see Audit Logs.” (Only show second sentence if feature enabled.)

Empty/error states
- If metrics are delayed: timeline still renders step transitions, but shows “Metrics pending” badges with last update time.
- If an event lacks an actor (legacy/backfill): show “Unknown actor” with tooltip.
- If user lacks permission: show timeline read-only; actions hidden; activity still visible.

Edge cases (from beta + SRE feedback)
- Metric evaluation timeout caused step to appear ‘stuck’: timeline should show a ‘Needs attention’ callout with suggested actions (retry evaluation / pause / rollback) and a “Last evaluation attempt” timestamp.
- Split mismatch by region (enforcement lag): show a warning banner “Traffic split not fully applied in all regions yet” with region-level status (collapsed by default). Avoid listing per-AZ.
- Streaming retries: do not show “double-counted” step transitions; activity is based on orchestrator events only.

Accessibility + internationalization
- Timeline must be navigable via keyboard; state indicated via both color and text.
- Use consistent badge shapes for status.
- Timestamps in user locale; show UTC on hover.

Deliverables
- Figma: rollout timeline step cards, approval checkpoint row, banners for auto events, and activity feed patterns
- Interaction spec: state transitions and action availability matrix by status + permission
- Copy deck for auto-pause/rollback reasons + destructive confirmations

Links
- Wizard flow: DES-742
- Metrics view: DES-763
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd.json
- Design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/hosted-canary-rollout-workflow-design-spec.json
- Audit events spec: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-events-rollout-actions.json

Open questions
1) Do we show ‘auto-paused’ and ‘auto-rolled back’ as separate terminal statuses, or show status + last event? Current recommendation: status is the state; events explain the reason.
2) Should activity include policy/permission denials? Proposed: only when a user attempted an action (so it’s traceable), not for background policy evaluations.
3) Should approvals appear in both Timeline and Activity? Proposed: yes (Timeline shows current checkpoint; Activity is the record).
4) Do we allow adding a comment after an auto-pause to document decision-making? Proposed: add “Add note” action (non-audit) if easy; otherwise GA follow-up.

Acceptance criteria
- A customer can answer: What step are we on? What percent is canary? How long have we been soaking? Why are we paused? Who approved? When did rollback happen?
- Timeline reflects all major lifecycle transitions in a human-readable way.
- Activity entries map cleanly to audit events (ENG-9171) and include a stable event ID when available.
- Works in read-only mode for users without rollout permissions.",
  "comments": [
    "2025-02-21 (Tessa Morgan): Spinning this off from DES-742. Beta feedback: customers loved the wizard but had no confidence post-start; they want a ‘flight recorder’ view. Need tight alignment with audit events + orchestrator state machine.",
    "2025-02-24 (Kenji Nakamura): Draft IA: Rollout details page with Timeline + Metrics + Activity. Question: do we make Activity a right-side panel on Timeline to reduce navigation? Testing both options in Figma.",
    "2025-02-26 (Marissa Cole): +1 on activity being visible without audit-log entitlement, but language must avoid promising compliance-grade logs. Also want an approval checkpoint row that’s obvious (some customers missed approval gates in other workflows).",
    "2025-02-28 (Marcus Lin): Please ensure we can display ‘Audit Event ID’ (or link) when Audit Logs are enabled. Also: actor should include auth principal type (user vs service account) if we support service accounts initiating rollouts.",
    "2025-03-03 (Sean Gallagher): For auto-pause/rollback, we need reason text that’s actionable and non-alarming. Ex: “p95 latency exceeded threshold” + show window + observed values. Avoid internal metric names like ‘rw.http.server.latency.p95’.",
    "2025-03-06 (Nora Ahmed): Implementation note: timeline needs a ‘system’ row type that isn’t a step. Orchestrator emits events that don’t correspond 1:1 to steps (e.g., evaluation retries). Design should support that without confusing customers.",
    "2025-03-11 (Kenji Nakamura): Added ‘Needs attention’ banner for metric-eval timeout / stuck conditions. Banner includes: last evaluation attempt, suggested next actions, and link to runbook (internal only). Need to confirm what’s customer-facing.",
    "2025-03-14 (Felix Schneider): For Activity diffs, avoid showing raw JSON in the feed; show compact diffs with a ‘View config’ drawer for full detail. This helps keep the feed readable and reduces risk of leaking internal fields.",
    "2025-03-18 (Tessa Morgan): Copy review based on design Slack thread: prefer ‘Auto-paused’ (temporary) vs ‘Auto-rolled back’ (destructive). Add confirmation modal copy for manual rollback requiring a reason/comment (stored in Activity).",
    "2025-03-21 (Kenji Nakamura): Marking In Review. Figma links shared in #design for review. Pending: finalize region-scope warning pattern (split mismatch) and the wording for ‘Unknown actor’/legacy events."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_6b8cf1a56ff7450cae5a435ab6499c28"
}

document.title: GA launch criteria + beta exit checklist — Hosted canary rollouts
document.content:
{
  "key": "PM-1859",
  "team": "product-management",
  "title": "GA launch criteria + beta exit checklist — Hosted canary rollouts",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2025-02-20",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-22",
  "creator": "Paula Mendes",
  "assignee": "Marissa Cole",
  "project": "Hosted Canary Rollout Workflow (GA)",
  "cycle": "2025-W12",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2025-04-04",
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "console-2025.04",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "labels": [
    "ga-readiness",
    "hosted",
    "rollouts",
    "console",
    "sre",
    "security",
    "docs",
    "support-enablement"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "PM-1843",
    "PM-1851",
    "ENG-9123",
    "ENG-9140",
    "ENG-9146",
    "ENG-9152",
    "ENG-9158",
    "ENG-9171",
    "ENG-9180",
    "DES-742",
    "DES-755",
    "DES-763"
  ],
  "sub_issues": [
    "Create GA go/no-go doc + signoff list (Console/Platform/SRE/Security/Support)",
    "Confirm default auto-stop thresholds by tier/region for GA",
    "Finalize customer-facing limitations/known issues section for docs",
    "Support macros + troubleshooting flow for auto-pause / split mismatch",
    "Run GA staging game day with stop/rollback + audit validation"
  ],
  "description": "Purpose
- Define the Beta Exit criteria and GA Launch checklist for the Hosted canary rollout workflow (percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes).
- Align Console, Control Plane, Smart Routing/Data Plane, Telemetry/SRE, Security, Docs, and Support on what “GA-ready” means.
- Serve as the single checklist for the GA go/no-go meeting and as a record of what we validated.

Scope reminder (GA)
- Hosted routes only (Dedicated/Private: schema-compatible, not GA)
- Console wizard to create/run/pause/rollback, plus timeline/activity view and cohort comparison metrics
- Policy guardrails: max step size, min soak time, approval gates (RBAC), auto-stop/auto-rollback based on SLO metrics
- Audit logging + customer-visible activity timeline

Beta Exit Criteria (must meet before scheduling GA)
1) Design partner validation
- Minimum: 5 design partners enabled, with at least 3 running a real production canary on Hosted.
- At least 10 completed rollouts end-to-end (create → start → step changes → reach 100% OR rollback).
- No P0/P1 issues open related to incorrect routing split, inability to rollback, or audit trail gaps.
- Qualitative: partners confirm they can understand (a) current step, (b) what will happen next, (c) why auto-stop occurred, and (d) how to rollback.

2) Reliability outcomes during beta
- No unresolved incidents attributable to rollout feature causing widespread request misrouting or outages.
- Any beta incidents have documented root cause, fix merged, and backported as needed (e.g., metric timeout stall bugfix; split mismatch learnings).
- SRE signoff that alerts are actionable and not generating sustained alert storms.

3) Governance + safety outcomes during beta
- Policy guardrails enforced consistently across UI and API (no bypass via API for restricted actions).
- Approval gates tested with RBAC role(s) (rollout-approver) and common enterprise setups.
- Audit events present for all required action types, with correct actor identity and diffs.

GA Launch Checklist (go/no-go)
A) Functional completeness (Console + API)
Owner: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin
- Wizard flow supports:
  - Selecting route, baseline model version/config, canary model version/config
  - Defining traffic schedule (step %, soak duration)
  - Configuring guardrails (max step size, min soak time) and showing validation errors clearly
  - Review + confirm with explicit warnings for destructive actions (rollback)
- Lifecycle actions supported and validated end-to-end:
  - Create rollout (draft)
  - Start rollout
  - Progress to next step (with/without approval gate)
  - Pause/resume
  - Rollback (manual) and “rollback to baseline” semantics
  - Auto-pause / auto-rollback on SLO breach (with reason surfaced)
- State machine correctness:
  - No “stuck” states on metric evaluation timeouts; clear retry + user-facing error
  - Idempotent retries for control plane → data plane propagation
- API parity for core operations (documented): create, get status, list activity, approve step, pause/resume, rollback

Acceptance evidence
- E2E test suite passing in CI and nightly (ENG-9164)
- Staging manual walkthrough recorded (link in go/no-go notes)

B) Smart Routing enforcement correctness
Owner: Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon
- Deterministic cohorting implemented and documented (hash inputs + stickiness rules)
- Percentage split accuracy within tolerance per region (define tolerance below)
- Correct behavior for:
  - Multi-region traffic
  - Streaming requests
  - Retries (client and internal)
  - Fallback routing interactions (baseline vs canary; precedence per ADR)
- Kill switch behavior verified:
  - Tenant-level disable immediately forces 100% baseline
  - Global disable forces baseline and prevents new rollouts from starting

Split accuracy target (GA)
- For stable traffic volume, measured canary proportion should converge to target within ±2% absolute over a 15-minute window (per region), excluding low-volume routes.
- For low volume routes, UI must display “insufficient volume” guidance instead of implying precise percentages.

Acceptance evidence
- Staging smoke tests (perf-canary PR-147)
- Post-fix validation for beta split mismatch scenario (see incident thread: rollout-split-mismatch-us-east)

C) Telemetry, dashboards, and alerting
Owner: Sean Gallagher / Aisha Bello / Logan Wright
Required cohort signals (tagging + aggregation)
- Every request must be attributable to:
  - route
  - model version/config (baseline vs canary)
  - cohort (baseline/canary)
  - region
  - rollout_id (with cardinality controls; ensure no blowups)
- Metrics required in Console comparison view + internal dashboards:
  - Request rate (RPS)
  - Error rate (overall, 5xx, timeouts)
  - Latency (p50/p95; ideally p99 in internal)
  - Tokens/sec and cost proxies (where available)
  - Streaming-specific failure modes (disconnects, partial completions) if tracked

Stop conditions (GA defaults)
- Auto-stop/auto-rollback must be available and enabled by default for new rollouts (with ability to tune thresholds by entitlement/tier).
- Default thresholds (initial GA proposal; finalize with SRE):
  - 5xx error rate: canary exceeds baseline by +1.0% absolute AND exceeds 2.0% absolute for 5 minutes
  - Timeout rate: canary exceeds baseline by +0.5% absolute for 5 minutes
  - p95 latency regression: canary p95 > baseline p95 * 1.25 for 10 minutes (guard for low volume)
- Rollout behavior on breach:
  - Auto-pause first if we can attribute breach confidently; auto-rollback when breach persists (or per policy)
  - Always emit: (1) customer-visible timeline entry, (2) audit event, (3) notification event

Alerting guidelines
- Alerts should page SRE only for:
  - Routing enforcement drift/incorrectness
  - Orchestrator stuck rollouts at scale
  - Global cohort tagging failures
  - Control plane → data plane propagation failures
- Customer route-specific canary SLO breaches should notify customer in Console/timeline and optionally via webhook/email (no paging unless systemic).

Acceptance evidence
- Cohort dashboards exist + validated against known traffic patterns (PR-28910 / observability pack PR-184)
- Cardinality analysis completed and within limits (Drive: rollout-cohort-metrics-cardinality-analysis)

D) Audit logging + change history (Security/Compliance)
Owner: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei
Required audit event coverage
- Events must be emitted for:
  - rollout.created
  - rollout.started
  - rollout.step.approval_requested
  - rollout.step.approved / rollout.step.denied
  - rollout.step.changed (percent change)
  - rollout.paused / rollout.resumed
  - rollout.rolled_back (manual)
  - rollout.auto_paused / rollout.auto_rolled_back (include stop condition + metric snapshot reference)
  - rollout.completed
- Required fields (high level): tenant_id, actor_id/actor_type, route_id, rollout_id, previous_state → new_state, diff (human readable + structured), timestamp, request_id/trace_id when applicable.
- Retention and export:
  - Align with existing audit log retention policy by tier
  - Verify SIEM export compatibility (field naming and size limits)

Customer-visible activity timeline
- Must match audit events but may exclude security-only internal fields; should show “what happened” and “why” (e.g., auto-pause reason).

Acceptance evidence
- Security review of audit event schema doc (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)
- Sample events captured in staging and validated by Security (screenshots/log dumps referenced in go/no-go)

E) Policy guardrails + RBAC
Owner: Jordan Lee / Kaitlyn Nguyen
- Guardrails enforced for step changes:
  - Max step size (e.g., 1% → 50% disallowed without override/approval)
  - Minimum soak time before next step
  - Approval gates configurable by tenant/admin policy
- Entitlement mapping documented:
  - Which customers get auto-rollback, approvals, advanced retention, etc.
- RBAC roles validated:
  - Who can create rollouts
  - Who can start/pause/rollback
  - Who can approve (rollout-approver role)
- UI error messaging must reflect policy engine errors with actionable guidance (e.g., “Wait 20m more to satisfy min soak”)

Acceptance evidence
- Policy engine tests and Console integration tests pass (PR-28802)
- Manual validation with at least 2 common enterprise role setups

F) Documentation (public + internal)
Owner: Elliot Price / Wei Chen
Customer docs must include
- Conceptual overview: baseline vs canary, cohorting, step schedule, soak time
- Step-by-step Console walkthrough
- API reference (or links) for rollout operations
- Troubleshooting:
  - Why a rollout auto-paused
  - Why metrics show “insufficient volume”
  - Split mismatch debugging steps (what to check before contacting support)
  - How to rollback safely
- Limitations (GA):
  - No bandits/dynamic optimization
  - Quality gates optional/manual (not hard gates)
  - Dedicated/Private not GA

Internal docs must include
- Enablement how-to (feature flags, permissions, sanity checks)
- On-call runbook for stuck rollout / bad split
- Release/change management checklist

Acceptance evidence
- Docs PR merged (redwood-docs PR-922)
- Runbooks published (Confluence) and reviewed with SRE + Support

G) Support readiness + incident response
Owner: Dev Patel / Rafael Mendes
- Support playbooks:
  - Triage flow for “rollout paused unexpectedly after latency spike”
  - Triage flow for “traffic split not matching config”
  - Escalation path to on-call / engineering
  - What data to request: tenant_id, route, rollout_id, timeframe, region, request IDs
- Macros/snippets created for common questions (e.g., “How do I do a percentage rollout on Hosted route?”)
- SLA for response during GA launch week and ownership for escalation channel

Acceptance evidence
- At least 2 support training sessions run (recording link in go/no-go)
- Sample tickets resolved using new macros (reference: SUP-48211, SUP-48302, SUP-48377)

H) Release management + staged rollout plan
Owner: Connor O'Brien / Soojin Lee
- Feature flags:
  - Per-tenant enablement
  - Internal dogfood tenants first
  - Staged cohort of beta → expanded beta → GA default (if applicable)
  - Kill switch playbook (owners + steps)
- Migration/backward compatibility validated for config schema changes
- Backout strategy:
  - Disable canary UI
  - Force baseline routing
  - Preserve audit logs and rollout history for completed rollouts

Acceptance evidence
- Change management checklist completed (Drive: hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist)
- Release readiness review held 48–72 hours pre-GA

Go/No-Go Process (how we decide)
Meeting: GA Readiness Review (60 minutes)
Required attendees / signoffs
- Product: Marissa Cole (final call)
- Console Eng: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin
- Platform/Policy: Ethan Park / Jordan Lee
- Smart Routing: Mina Haddad
- SRE: Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes
- Security: Marcus Lin
- Docs/Support: Elliot Price + Dev Patel

Decision rules
- No-go if any of:
  - Known issue causing incorrect split enforcement at material rates
  - Rollback unavailable or unreliable
  - Missing audit events for any action type listed above
  - Unbounded metrics cardinality risk unresolved
  - No validated kill switch
- Conditional go allowed if:
  - Minor UI polish issues only
  - Non-blocking docs follow-ups with explicit owner + date
  - Non-paging alert tuning improvements queued (does not impact safety)

Artifacts to attach in go/no-go notes
- Links: PRD, design spec, ADRs
- Latest beta partner tracker snapshot
- List of open bugs (P0/P1 only) with owners + ETA
- Staging game day results + any follow-ups

Current status / open questions (as of last update)
- Need final agreement on GA default thresholds by region/tier; beta feedback suggests p95 multiplier threshold may be too aggressive for long-context routes.
- Confirm whether GA requires customer notifications beyond Console timeline (e.g., webhook). If not in GA, docs must state Console-only.
- Ensure “insufficient volume” guidance text matches design copy and does not confuse customers about split accuracy.

Links
- Confluence PRD: hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd
- Confluence design spec: hosted-canary-rollout-workflow-design-spec
- ADR: adr-hosted-rollout-cohorting-and-traffic-splitting
- ADR: adr-rollout-policy-evaluation-order-and-precedence
- Runbook: runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split
- SLO/alerts: hosted-rollouts-slo-metrics-and-alerts
- Docs PR: redwood-docs PR-922
- Observability: observability-pack PR-184",
  "comments": [
    "2025-02-24 (Paula Mendes): Drafted initial checklist structure. Pulled in audit event requirements from Security and stop-condition needs from SRE. Need owners to confirm default thresholds for GA vs per-tier overrides.",
    "2025-03-03 (Sean Gallagher): Added alerting guidance: route-specific cohort regressions should not page by default; page only for systemic tagging/enforcement/control-plane propagation issues. Request: ensure kill switch is tested in a game day prior to GA.",
    "2025-03-06 (Marcus Lin): Audit events list looks complete. Please ensure actor identity is consistent across Console and API actions (service-to-service calls should still attribute initiating user). Also confirm retention/export constraints are unchanged vs existing audit log product.",
    "2025-03-10 (Dylan Brooks): Console timeline view will surface auto-pause/auto-rollback reasons + link to cohort comparison metrics. Need final copy for low-volume/insufficient-volume states (Design thread pending).",
    "2025-03-14 (Marissa Cole): Updating Beta Exit criteria to require 3 production design partners (not just staging). Added explicit no-go rules (split correctness, rollback reliability, audit coverage).",
    "2025-03-18 (Rafael Mendes): Please add explicit runbook validation step: support should be able to follow runbook to diagnose “bad split” and collect required logs/IDs without engineering involvement. Also note that we saw one beta case where metric evaluation timeouts stalled a rollout; ensure fix is included in GA bundle.",
    "2025-03-22 (Paula Mendes): Incorporated beta learnings: split mismatch incident and metric timeout stall. Added split accuracy tolerance language and clarified that low-volume routes should show guidance vs precise claims."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_5444ca17e9664747930ead86571d4804"
}

    "content": "{\n  \"channel\": \"product\",\n  \"thread_ts\": \"1719672000\",\n  \"first_message_ts\": \"1719672000\",\n  \"last_message_ts\": \"1719675600\",\n  \"participants\": [\n    \"Maya (Product)\",\n    \"Alex (Eng-Platform)\",\n    \"Priya (Eng-Observability)\",\n    \"Jordan (Eng-ML)\",\n    \"Casey (PM)\",\n    \"Nina (Design)\",\n    \"infra-bot\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": \"Maya (Product): quick kickoff \\u2014 we need to align on the observability roadmap for Q3: dashboards, tracing hooks, cost breakdown, and error analytics. customer asks piled up, so we need hard tradeoffs.\\nAlex (Eng-Platform): agree. can we list must-haves vs nice-to-haves? perf overhead is a big gating factor.\\nPriya (Eng-Observability): must-haves from infra POV: 1) per-route latency p50/p95/p99, 2) per-model token cost breakdown, 3) trace hooks that don't add >5% p95.\\nCasey (PM): customer asks: two large customers want per-request cost tags and sampling control for traces, both for Dedicated and Private. they said release readiness depends on that.\\nJordan (Eng-ML): for per-token cost we need KV cache visibility + batch attribution. that's an implementation effort across runtime and console. estimate ~3 sprint work.\\nNina (Design): dashboards should ship with three starter views: overview (SLOs + costs), queryable traces, and error heatmap. low visual complexity to start.\\nMaya (Product): launch criteria proposal: 1) dashboard templates (overview + latency + cost) 2) trace hook with sampling config and minimal baggage 3) alerting for error rate regressions 4) perf overhead validated <5% on a 3-model mix. thoughts?\\nAlex (Eng-Platform): sounds reasonable. add rollout policy: start hosted beta -> Dedicated customers opt-in -> Private GA. That reduces blast radius.\\nPriya (Eng-Observability): technical note: trace hook API: \\n```\\nPOST /v1/trace-hooks {\\n  sample_rate: 0.1,\\n  include_prefixes: [\\\"/v1/chat\\\", \\\"/v1/embed\\\"],\\n  tags: [\\\"model\\\",\\\"route\\\",\\\"customer_id\\\"]\\n}\\n```\\nThis keeps payload small. sample_rate must be configurable per-customer.\\nCasey (PM): customers also asked for cost breakdown by model variant and quantization level. add as stretch goal.\\nJordan (Eng-ML): quantization-level cost attribution is doable if runtime emits model_variant metadata on request. minor runtime change + console mapping. estimate 1 sprint for telemetry, 1 sprint for console.\\nMaya (Product): OK. prioritize per-request cost tags and sampling control as MVP. quantization/variant cost as M1.\\nNina (Design): quick UX question: do we show cost as absolute $$ or normalized token-cost units? customers requested both.\\nAlex (Eng-Platform): show both. $$ requires billing linkups (edge case for Private). token-cost units are safer for Private.\\nPriya (Eng-Observability): data retention: default 30 days for traces, 90 days for metrics. Private customers may request longer via config. note: retention affects storage costs a lot.\\nMaya (Product): acceptance criteria checklist for launch:\\n- Dashboard templates exist and are editable\\n- Trace hook API implemented and docs + examples\\n- Per-request cost tags emitted and visible in UI\\n- Error analytics: grouping + root-cause drilldowns (basic)\\n- Performance overhead tests + signoff\\n- Rollout plan documented\\nCan someone own the list items?\\nAlex (Eng-Platform): I'll own runtime + perf tests.\\nPriya (Eng-Observability): I'll own trace hook API + storage plan.\\nCasey (PM): I'll coordinate docs + customer comms + beta signups.\\nNina (Design): I'll prototype dashboard templates by EOW and hand off to frontend.\\nJordan (Eng-ML): I'll add model_variant metadata and batching attribution hooks.\\nMaya (Product): timeline proposal: 6 weeks for MVP (two sprints). if we scope down further to hit 4 weeks we drop the error RCA and quantization-cost mapping. prefer to commit 6 weeks.\\nAlex (Eng-Platform): 6 weeks is tight but doable with focused scope. need two dedicated engs full-time.\\nPriya (Eng-Observability): risk: Private installs with strict network constraints may need an offline metrics shipper. that's a +2 week unknown.\\nCasey (PM): mitigation: document Private constraints and offer a 'limited feature' compatibility matrix for GA.\\nMaya (Product): decision: go for 6-week MVP, prioritize per-request cost, sampling control, and dashboard templates. RCA and quantization-cost = M1.\\nNina (Design): noted. I'll mock templates for beta flows and include a compact mobile view.\\ninfra-bot: deploy-bot noted: created epic OBS-4321 and linked PR template.\\nMaya (Product): next steps: Alex & Priya to write tech spec by Tues, Casey to start customer beta invites, Nina to upload mocks. we'll sync Thurs 10am.\\nAlex (Eng-Platform): will do. tagging @Priya for spec sync.\\nPriya (Eng-Observability): on it. adding perf test matrix to the spec.\\nCasey (PM): adding two customer contacts to beta list: AcmeAI and FinLedger. both require Dedicated support.\\nJordan (Eng-ML): quick question: do we need to expose sampling controls to customers via API or console only?\\nMaya (Product): both. console control for beta, API control by GA.\\nAlex (Eng-Platform): note: exposes an admin API + RBAC checks. add to spec.\\nMaya (Product): awesome. thanks everyone \\u2014 see you Thu 10am. :tada:\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_16f5a1cc914d4b8f8070a0f4031b7210\"\n}",

document.title: 1719672000 kickoff instrumentation priorities roadmap
document.content:
{
  "channel": "product",
  "thread_ts": "1719672000",
  "first_message_ts": "1719672000",
  "last_message_ts": "1719675600",
  "participants": [
    "Maya (Product)",
    "Alex (Eng-Platform)",
    "Priya (Eng-Observability)",
    "Jordan (Eng-ML)",
    "Casey (PM)",
    "Nina (Design)",
    "infra-bot"
  ],
  "messages": "Maya (Product): quick kickoff — we need to align on the observability roadmap for Q3: dashboards, tracing hooks, cost breakdown, and error analytics. customer asks piled up, so we need hard tradeoffs.
Alex (Eng-Platform): agree. can we list must-haves vs nice-to-haves? perf overhead is a big gating factor.
Priya (Eng-Observability): must-haves from infra POV: 1) per-route latency p50/p95/p99, 2) per-model token cost breakdown, 3) trace hooks that don't add >5% p95.
Casey (PM): customer asks: two large customers want per-request cost tags and sampling control for traces, both for Dedicated and Private. they said release readiness depends on that.
Jordan (Eng-ML): for per-token cost we need KV cache visibility + batch attribution. that's an implementation effort across runtime and console. estimate ~3 sprint work.
Nina (Design): dashboards should ship with three starter views: overview (SLOs + costs), queryable traces, and error heatmap. low visual complexity to start.
Maya (Product): launch criteria proposal: 1) dashboard templates (overview + latency + cost) 2) trace hook with sampling config and minimal baggage 3) alerting for error rate regressions 4) perf overhead validated <5% on a 3-model mix. thoughts?
Alex (Eng-Platform): sounds reasonable. add rollout policy: start hosted beta -> Dedicated customers opt-in -> Private GA. That reduces blast radius.
Priya (Eng-Observability): technical note: trace hook API: 
```
POST /v1/trace-hooks {
  sample_rate: 0.1,
  include_prefixes: ["/v1/chat", "/v1/embed"],
  tags: ["model","route","customer_id"]
}
```
This keeps payload small. sample_rate must be configurable per-customer.
Casey (PM): customers also asked for cost breakdown by model variant and quantization level. add as stretch goal.
Jordan (Eng-ML): quantization-level cost attribution is doable if runtime emits model_variant metadata on request. minor runtime change + console mapping. estimate 1 sprint for telemetry, 1 sprint for console.
Maya (Product): OK. prioritize per-request cost tags and sampling control as MVP. quantization/variant cost as M1.
Nina (Design): quick UX question: do we show cost as absolute $$ or normalized token-cost units? customers requested both.
Alex (Eng-Platform): show both. $$ requires billing linkups (edge case for Private). token-cost units are safer for Private.
Priya (Eng-Observability): data retention: default 30 days for traces, 90 days for metrics. Private customers may request longer via config. note: retention affects storage costs a lot.
Maya (Product): acceptance criteria checklist for launch:
- Dashboard templates exist and are editable
- Trace hook API implemented and docs + examples
- Per-request cost tags emitted and visible in UI
- Error analytics: grouping + root-cause drilldowns (basic)
- Performance overhead tests + signoff
- Rollout plan documented
Can someone own the list items?
Alex (Eng-Platform): I'll own runtime + perf tests.
Priya (Eng-Observability): I'll own trace hook API + storage plan.
Casey (PM): I'll coordinate docs + customer comms + beta signups.
Nina (Design): I'll prototype dashboard templates by EOW and hand off to frontend.
Jordan (Eng-ML): I'll add model_variant metadata and batching attribution hooks.
Maya (Product): timeline proposal: 6 weeks for MVP (two sprints). if we scope down further to hit 4 weeks we drop the error RCA and quantization-cost mapping. prefer to commit 6 weeks.
Alex (Eng-Platform): 6 weeks is tight but doable with focused scope. need two dedicated engs full-time.
Priya (Eng-Observability): risk: Private installs with strict network constraints may need an offline metrics shipper. that's a +2 week unknown.
Casey (PM): mitigation: document Private constraints and offer a 'limited feature' compatibility matrix for GA.
Maya (Product): decision: go for 6-week MVP, prioritize per-request cost, sampling control, and dashboard templates. RCA and quantization-cost = M1.
Nina (Design): noted. I'll mock templates for beta flows and include a compact mobile view.
infra-bot: deploy-bot noted: created epic OBS-4321 and linked PR template.
Maya (Product): next steps: Alex & Priya to write tech spec by Tues, Casey to start customer beta invites, Nina to upload mocks. we'll sync Thurs 10am.
Alex (Eng-Platform): will do. tagging @Priya for spec sync.
Priya (Eng-Observability): on it. adding perf test matrix to the spec.
Casey (PM): adding two customer contacts to beta list: AcmeAI and FinLedger. both require Dedicated support.
Jordan (Eng-ML): quick question: do we need to expose sampling controls to customers via API or console only?
Maya (Product): both. console control for beta, API control by GA.
Alex (Eng-Platform): note: exposes an admin API + RBAC checks. add to spec.
Maya (Product): awesome. thanks everyone — see you Thu 10am. :tada:",
